articles.title: The new BJP team’s piecemeal reset
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Apart from the usual distribution of organisational berths to poll-going States, caste groups, and other demographics of sex and age, the new BJP team reflects the party’s attempts at a reset. Nistula Hebbar reports on how three terms in power have brought both the pieties of the past and anxieties of the future into focus

Prime Minister Narendra Modi walked into a meeting of the newly appointed Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national office-bearers on August 22. The 64 office-bearers present assumed he would address them on how they should approach their assignments. Instead, he spent the next four-and-a-quarter hours individually querying them on their past organisational work.

The exchange was unhurried, with PM Modi at one point telling the audience that he too was once like them, a national office-bearer of the party during the late Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s tenure as Prime Minister (1999-2004), say some of the new office-bearers.

The identification was interpreted in some quarters as a pep talk to the new team of how far organisational service can take you in the BJP, but for others it pointed to a unifying characteristic in a list of names that otherwise lacked a meta narrative, and instead, in a piecemeal fashion exhibited the political anxieties of the BJP.

This privileging of organisational experience by the Prime Minister was the highlight of the new team. The BJP, now in its third term in power and seeking a fourth in 2029, is, with this new team, attempting a reset amid various political anxieties.

Journalist Shekhar Iyer, who has tracked the BJP for decades, says, “The new team marks a big shift in the party top brass’ approach to the challenges ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha poll. Increasingly, the BJP is signalling to itself that, henceforth, the chosen men and women will represent less of their individual personality and more of their abilities and capabilities for the tasks to be accomplished.”

articles.title: BJP appoints Yuzvendra Chahal as special invitee to OBC Morcha executive committee
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: BJP national president Nitin Nabin on November 21, 2026, announced fresh appointments of national office-bearers, national executive members, and department heads for its OBC Morcha with immediate effect
Indian cricketer Yuzvendra Chahal has been appointed as a Special Invitee to the Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) National Other Backwards Classes (OBC) Morcha executive committee.

BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Saturday (November 21, 2026) announced fresh appointments of national office-bearers, national executive members, and department heads for its OBC Morcha with immediate effect.

According to the official communication issued by the party’s central office, the list includes seven national vice presidents, three national general secretaries, and seven national secretaries representing various states across the country.

The seven newly appointed national vice presidents of the BJP OBC Morcha are Jogen Mohan (Assam), Mamata Mohanta (Odisha), Sangam Lal Gupta (Uttar Pradesh), Babanrao Ravji Choudhary (Maharashtra), Sat Prakash Rana (Delhi), Arjun Sahani (Bihar), and Sangeeta Balwant Bind (Uttar Pradesh). Gajendra Yadav (Delhi), Pramod Madhwaraj (Karnataka), and Lalit Chandrakar (Chhattisgarh) have been named as national general secretaries.

The party also appointed seven national secretaries: Dashrathji Thakor (Gujarat), T Varatharajan (Tamil Nadu), Sanjeev Kumar alias Bablu Bhagat (Jharkhand), Sarita Jangid (Haryana), Kadaganchi Ramesh (Telangana), Vaibhav Panwar (Madhya Pradesh), and Bhim Kumar Sahu (Bihar). Under the organisational appointments, Radheshyam Yadav from Uttar Pradesh has been given charge as the national treasurer. Sanjay Kumar Gurjar and Dr Arun Yadav (both from Delhi) have been appointed as national office secretary and co-office secretary, respectively.

Ajay Gupta from Bihar has been named the media coordinator for the Morcha. For digital communication, Parikshit Dagar (Delhi) has been appointed social media coordinator, with Pradeep Mahaur Soni (Madhya Pradesh) named co-coordinator.
Prof. Pankaj Choudhary (Delhi) will head the policy and research wing as coordinator, assisted by co-coordinators Ashutosh Behera (Odisha) and Rahul Yadav (Uttar Pradesh).

The party also notified the initial names of the national executive committee members, including Sanjeev Rangaiya (Andaman & Nicobar), Srinivas Rao Kantubukta (Andhra Pradesh), Rajiv Ranjan alias Vishal Yadav (Bihar), and Sanjeev Verma (Chandigarh).

articles.title: Palaniswami criticises TVK-led government over SC dismissal of TN’s Cauvery pleas
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a social media post, Palaniswami claimed the CM was not aware of the Supreme Court’s decision

AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami on Sunday (November 22, 2026) criticised the Tamil Nadu government, led by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, after the Supreme Court dismissed two applications filed by the State in connection with the Cauvery water dispute.
In a social media post, Mr. Palaniswami claimed the CM was not aware of the Supreme Court’s decision. .

“You (Mr Vijay) will not convene an all-party meeting over the Cauvery dispute. You will not engage with the Congress leadership on the issue or pursue the legal battle effectively. And you will pose for photographs without condemning Karnataka CM, who has been speaking against Tamil Nadu,” Mr. Palaniswami said.

The AIADMK leader warned the inadequate release of Cauvery water by Karnataka along with the “TVK-led alliance government’s failure” to secure Tamil Nadu’s rightful share, could adversely affect the samba cultivation season.

Questioning the Chief Minister’s priorities, Mr. Palaniswami charged that the CM had failed to raise the concerns of Tamil Nadu’s farmers during his recent meeting with Congress leader Sonia Gandhi in New Delhi. [Mr Vijay had gone to attend a function to mark the launch of Ms Gandhi’s memoirs.]

Mr. Vijay was playing with the rights linked with the lifeline of Tamil Nadu and the lives of the farmers in the State, Mr. Palaniswami said. Recalling the AIADMK’s efforts under former CMs M.G. Ramachandran, Jayalalithaa and himself, Mr. Palaniswami contended the party had fought to secure the State’s Cauvery rights over the Cauvery issue.

articles.title: Congress hopeful of U.P. alliance with SP, seeks ‘respectable’ seat-sharing
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘We were weak, but we are not weak now. We have the best leader in this country right now, as only we can handle the BJP better than any other party,’ says Rajendra Pal Gautam

The Congress is hopeful of forging an alliance with the Samajwadi Party (SP) for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election but wants a “respectable” seat-sharing arrangement, All India Congress Committee in-charge for the State Rajendra Pal Gautam has said.

Mr. Gautam, in an interview with The Hindu , said the two parties are expected to hold formal seat-sharing discussions this week and asserted that the Congress would make the alleged “ chanda chori ” (theft of temple donations) a major campaign issue.

Though he did not disclose the exact date, the first meeting is likely to be held on Monday afternoon. Senior leaders, including Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, K.C. Venugopal, and Mr. Gautam, are expected to participate.

Commenting on SP chief Akhilesh Yadav’s recent statement that the Congress had sought 181 seats, Mr. Gautam said, “I am not going to reveal which seats, but we have given them a list. We will try to convince them, and I am sure they will try to convince us. The outcome depends on these talks.”
Asked whether the Congress would settle for an alliance at any cost, Mr. Gautam said: “It is not like that at all. The understanding will be a respectable one.”

Countering suggestions that the Congress lacked the organisational strength to bargain for a substantial share of seats, Mr. Gautam pointed out that while the SP won 37 seats and the Congress six in the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the SP’s alliance with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) in the 2019 Lok Sabha polls had not yielded similar results.
“We were weak, but we are not weak now,” he said, adding, “We have the best leader in this country right now, as only we can handle the BJP better than any other party.”

articles.title: Plan approach paper eyes leveraging heft of Keralam’s economy for 15th Five-Year Plan period
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The UDF government and the Planning Board have visualised a ‘partnership economy’ for building the economy up from ₹16 lakh crore to ₹28 lakh crore by 2031-32

In targeting a 7% growth in real terms during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2027-2032), the UDF government is hoping to leverage the heft of Keralam’s economy, which, according to the State Planning Board’s approach paper to the 15th Plan, “contains far more capital than its government commands.”

Real growth of 7% a year for five years (2027-2032) at the incremental capital-output ratio (the measure of how much investment is needed to generate a unit of economic growth) of around 4, implies investment of ₹4.5 lakh crore a year, according to the approach paper. The 2026-27 Revised Budget on the other hand estimates a capital expenditure of only ₹22,566 crore. “About ₹19 in ₹20 of the investment Keralam needs will therefore come from outside the State Budget,” the paper, published last week, notes.

On money outside the Budget, the approach paper has this to say: “Bank deposits stand at ₹10,84,241 crore and advances at ₹7,81,043 crore, a credit-deposit ratio of 72.04%. Non-resident deposits are ₹2,86,063 crore. Primary agricultural credit societies hold nearly ₹1.3 lakh crore, about 70% of all such deposits in the country. Remittances were ₹2,16,893 crore in 2023. Bank lending depends on the availability of bankable projects, so the gap between deposits and advances measures the shortage of bankable projects in the State more than any shortage of savings. If credit to the Plan’s engines rose by the equivalent of 8% points of deposits, about ₹87,000 crore more would be at work in Keralam, nearly four times the annual capital budget.”
The task of planning will therefore be to direct that capital to productive use within the State, according to the paper.
The UDF government and the Planning Board have visualised a ‘partnership economy’ for building the economy up from ₹16 lakh crore to ₹28 lakh crore by 2031-32.

The approach paper to the 14th Five-Year Plan had noted that mobilising resources for the Plan period (2022-2027) would be a “challenging task.” The scenario has not changed much. The White Paper on Keralam’s fiscal health laid in the Legislative Assembly in June this year had observed that “behind Keralam’s social achievements lies a fiscal structure that is under serious and growing strain.”

The approach paper for the 15th Plan draws a grim picture of present-day Keralam. The State is a “picture of slow growth, low investment, large youth unemployment and an ageing population. The State’s fiscal space is rather limited, and its revenue base is weak. There is no hope of large Union transfers.”

articles.title: CJP plans to take ‘Cockroach Club’ across India, shifts youth movement beyond street protests
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Launched in Pune with over 300 participants, the initiative will combine political debates, lectures, film screenings, comedy and cultural performances as the party seeks to channelise youth energy into shaping India’s future

Moving beyond street mobilisation, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) is looking to build a nationwide network of cultural and discussion spaces with its newly launched ‘Cockroach Club’. The party wants the initiative to reach every part of the country, including remote villages, as it seeks to give young people a platform to debate public issues, exchange ideas and envision the future they want for India, its co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka said during an interaction with The Hindu.

The club’s first gathering, titled ‘Legacy of Bapu’, was held in Pune on November 21 and brought together more than 300 people for an event lasting around three hours. The programme featured comedy, satire and conversations on Mahatma Gandhi, while participants discussed local issues concerning Maharashtra. Performances addressing larger issues facing the country were also part of the event.

“This is a platform where we can all come together and articulate the future we want for ourselves and answer some difficult questions we want to address. The idea of Cockroach Clubs is to have a space where people can come, talk, brainstorm, collaborate and envision what they want our country to be,” Mr. Ranka said.

Explaining why Pune was chosen for the first gathering, he said the party had a large support base in Maharashtra, while Delhi was also an important centre for the organisation and would soon feature in its plans.
“The idea is for the Cockroach Club to go to every corner of the country. This is a truly national movement and everything has to come together,” he added.

CJP co-convenor Saurav Das said the club was envisioned as a “physical space for the younger generation” to come together, exchange ideas, question, learn and grow. It would host lectures and discussions on the ideas of Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, B.R. Ambedkar and other thinkers, besides film screenings, live performances and stand-up comedy.
The space would also offer young people a quiet corner to read, study, and prepare for examinations, while allowing them to unwind and interact, he said.

“This was just a trailer. As we go ahead, we will know what can be bettered. We will use this platform to discuss how to take this movement forward, how to get more and more people to join, and channelise the energy of the youth in a structured manner to bring a change in the country,” Mr. Das said.

He said the club would encourage young people to think for themselves rather than have opinions handed down to them or ideologies imposed on them. “We the young will develop our Idea of India at the Cockroach Club,” he said.
Over 300 people gathered at the Gandhi Bhavan, Kothrud in Pune for Cockroach Club’s first gathering, titled ‘Legacy of Bapu’, was held in Pune on November 21. Photo credit: Special Arrangement.

The first event was not ticketed, Mr. Ranka said. The local Pune team initially pooled money to organise the event, followed by local fundraising. A collection was also made at the venue, where participants contributed to their capacity.
The party is yet to decide how it will fund the initiative as it expands. It could consider introducing tickets for future events or continue with the local fundraising model, he said.

articles.title: JKSSB exam cheating racket: Six more arrested; six government employees among accused
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police said the question paper was allegedly taken out of the examination centre, photographed and circulated among selected candidates through Telegram

Six more persons were arrested in the ongoing investigation into the Finance Accounts Assistant (FAA) examination conducted recently by Jammu & Kashmir Services Selection Board, taking the total arrests to 20, with police clarifying that the malpractice was confined to a specific examination centre and did not involve a paper leak.

The accused include six government employees, among them the alleged mastermind. Police said the question paper was allegedly taken out of the examination centre, photographed and circulated among selected candidates through Telegram.
14 arrested as J&K Police bust exam cheating racket; mobiles, wireless sets seized

The investigation has also revealed financial transactions of ₹1.80 lakh, of which ₹1.40 lakh has been recovered, while the accused had allegedly negotiated payments of ₹10–12 lakh from candidates in exchange for helping them clear the examination, Jammu Senior Superintendent of Police Joginder Singh said at a press conference in Jammu.

On November 15, police in Jammu arrested 14 suspects ahead of the FAA exam, “uncovering” a network that planned to transmit answers to select candidates inside the exam centres through electronic communication devices.
Several wireless radio sets were seized in the intelligence-based operation, three FIRs were lodged, and a Special Investigation Team (SIT) was constituted to probe the alleged conspiracy.

Disclosing details of the investigation, the SSP said the probe had led to the identification and arrest of the alleged main kingpin, whose interrogation brought to light a wider network involving candidates, government employees and other intermediaries.

"Of the 20 persons arrested so far, six are government employees. Their details have been shared with the respective departments for departmental action. At the same time, criminal proceedings are also being pursued based on their alleged roles," he said, clarifying that none of the arrested persons belonged to the JKSSB.
According to the investigation, Mr. Singh said the alleged mastermind had initially planned to facilitate cheating for two persons — a close relative and a friend.

However, another accused involved in the operation allegedly created a separate network and contacted 20 to 22 additional candidates. He reportedly collected their original documents and obtained blank cheques from four to five candidates, with an understanding that payments would be made after they successfully cleared the examination.

Police said the question paper was accessed with the alleged assistance of an employee posted at the examination centre. After the examination began, papers placed on the desks of absent candidates were collected and taken to a designated room. “The employee allegedly removed one of the papers and handed it to another person, as he could not leave the examination centre,” the SSP said.

He said the second person then passed it on to an accused waiting outside, who allegedly took it to his car, photographed it and returned it for deposit at the centre. The photographs were subsequently circulated through a Telegram group to facilitate cheating by selected candidates.

On November 15, police in Jammu arrested 14 suspects ahead of the FAA exam, “uncovering” a network that planned to transmit answers to select candidates inside the exam centres through electronic communication devices.

Several wireless radio sets were seized in the intelligence-based operation, three FIRs were lodged, and a Special Investigation Team (SIT) was constituted to probe the alleged conspiracy.

Disclosing details of the investigation, the SSP said the probe had led to the identification and arrest of the alleged main kingpin, whose interrogation brought to light a wider network involving candidates, government employees and other intermediaries.

"Of the 20 persons arrested so far, six are government employees. Their details have been shared with the respective departments for departmental action. At the same time, criminal proceedings are also being pursued based on their alleged roles," he said, clarifying that none of the arrested persons belonged to the JKSSB.

According to the investigation, Mr. Singh said the alleged mastermind had initially planned to facilitate cheating for two persons — a close relative and a friend.

However, another accused involved in the operation allegedly created a separate network and contacted 20 to 22 additional candidates. He reportedly collected their original documents and obtained blank cheques from four to five candidates, with an understanding that payments would be made after they successfully cleared the examination.

Police said the question paper was accessed with the alleged assistance of an employee posted at the examination centre. After the examination began, papers placed on the desks of absent candidates were collected and taken to a designated room. “The employee allegedly removed one of the papers and handed it to another person, as he could not leave the examination centre,” the SSP said.

He said the second person then passed it on to an accused waiting outside, who allegedly took it to his car, photographed it and returned it for deposit at the centre. The photographs were subsequently circulated through a Telegram group to facilitate cheating by selected candidates.

articles.title: SCO Civilisational Dialogue ‘leaves options open’ for Pakistan SCO meets next year, say sources
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: As the government faces criticism over “inconsistency” in the invitation to Pakistan, officials say the invite can be seen as building a window of opportunity for “common civility”

The visit of Pakistan Minister for Environment and Climate Change, Musadik Malik, to India, the first by any senior Pakistani official since 2023, was a “Shanghai Cooperation Organisation” (SCO) initiative, not an Indian one alone, said officials as the government came under criticism from the Opposition.

However, former Indian diplomats who served in Pakistan said the visit and the invitation to the SCO Civilisational Dialogue in Delhi and the SCO Summit to be held in Pakistan next year could be seen as building a window of opportunity for “common civility” and providing a multilateral platform for the region, when bilateral moves, and the SAARC Summit are not taking place.

Ministry of External Affairs officials have stressed that there were no “bilateral” or one-to-one meetings during the three-day event hosted at Delhi’s iconic Purana Kila (Old Fort) monument. Ministers from six countries – Pakistan, Tajikistan, Nepal, Azerbaijan, Iran, and the Kyrgyz Republic – and Deputy Ministers from eight other countries participated in the forum.

Government officials pointed out that the event allows India a chance to highlight its cultural prowess and strong roots and furthers India’s common links with other members of the SCO, which also see themselves as “civilizational” states. It is also significant that India has carved out a space for itself in the year when Pakistan is the Chair of the SCO, they said, and is leading a shift in the grouping’s more security-oriented and land-locked focus to a more South Asian, oceanic and people-to-people linked focus.

They suggested that such meetings could also pave the way for next year, when External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will all be invited to Pakistan for SCO meetings chaired by Pakistan, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be invited to the Heads of Council meeting to be held in the third quarter of 2027. Government officials said it was too early to speak about participation in these meetings in Pakistan yet, but that a decision closer to the dates would only be possible if options were kept open at present, and SCO events in the run-up to the Summit are kept away from the “negativity” of bilateral relations.

“The meeting was in an SCO context so it would be inappropriate to read into it any bilateral content, leave alone a breakthrough,” said former Indian High Commissioner to Islamabad TCA Raghavan (2013-2015). He added, however, that “given the precarious and fraught state of India- Pakistan relations, an episode of common civility and normalcy is a plus and, even without intending to, creates possibilities.”

Former High Commissioner to Islamabad Ajay Bisaria (2017-2019), who was the last to serve in Pakistan before both sides downgraded ties in 2019, said that Mr. Malik’s visit to India represented “more than a formality but less than a thaw” and demonstrated how such multilateral events allow India and Pakistan to “tolerate each other’s presence, even when they won’t engage directly”. When asked about India’s attendance at SCO events in Pakistan next year, Mr. Bisaria said that the “ball is in Pakistan’s court” to “dial down both terrorism and rhetoric” if it hopes for Indian leaders to travel there. Significantly, he said such an event could be an opportunity to revive the SAARC process as well, that has been suspended for a decade.

On Friday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, making the point that while “empires had redrawn maps”, such dialogues had “transformed and enriched global thought”. Mr. Modi had proposed the Dialogue at the SCO Summit in Tianjin in 2025, and the proposal was adopted at the SCO Summit in Bishkek in October 2026, with the declaration announcing that it would be held in Delhi this month.

The criticism was particularly sharp over images this weekend of Mr. Modi and the Pakistani Minister seated in the first row, as well as of Culture Minister and host Gajendra Singh Shekhawat holding a conversation with Mr. Malik at a lunch table.

“This is a multilateral event within the SCO framework, for which invitations have been extended to all members of the SCO, including Pakistan,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, underlining at briefings held in the past week that the government has not changed its position on other outstanding bilateral issues with Pakistan including over the Pahalgam terror attack, and the suspension of the Indus Water Treaty.

India and Pakistan have at present no bilateral dialogue between them, and since 2016, when the Modi government decided to boycott SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation), they have dropped the regional engagement as well. However, New Delhi continues to make an exception for the SCO, founded in 1999 by Russia, China, and Central Asian states as a security forum to which India and Pakistan were inducted in 2017, and Iran and Belarus subsequently. In 2024, Mr. Jaishankar had travelled to Islamabad to represent India at the SCO Heads of Government Summit.

articles.title: India-EU trade pact likely to be signed on December 16
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: European Union's Ambassador to India, Jean-Eric Paquet, recently said the FTA will be signed during PM Modi's visit to Brussels in December, and it will come into force in 2027

India and the 27-nation bloc European Union (EU) are likely to sign the Free Trade Agreement (FTA) on December 16, an official said. The two sides concluded the negotiations for the pact on January 27 this year.

European Union's Ambassador to India, Jean-Eric Paquet, recently said the FTA will be signed during Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's visit to Brussels in December, and it will come into force next year.

The European Commission has already submitted proposals to the Council of the European Union seeking authorisation for signing and conclusion of the agreement, along with the final legal text and tariff schedules.

Under the free trade agreement, described as 'mother of all deals', 93 per cent of Indian shipments will enjoy duty-free access to the 27-nation bloc, while imports of luxury cars and wines from the EU will become less expensive.

The deal, concluded after negotiations spanning over two decades, will create a market of about 2 billion people across the world's fourth-largest economy, India, and the second-largest economic bloc, the EU.
Watch | India–EU Free Trade Agreement explained: Biggest trade deal in India’s history | India-New Zealand FTA comes into force; new visa categories for Indians, zero-duty access for exports
Taken together, India and the EU account for 25% of global GDP and one-third (about USD 11 trillion) of international trade (about $33 trillion).
The EU is India's largest trading partner in goods among individual blocs, while India ranks as the EU's ninth-largest goods trading partner globally and sixth in services.

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted Houthi missile in western region
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Saudi Arabia's western region contains key energy infrastructure including the Yanbu terminal, a major facility for crude oil exports
The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis said on Sunday (November 22, 2026) it had intercepted a ballistic missile launched toward the kingdom's western Red Sea coast.
"Air defence intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward the western region," coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki said in a social media post.

Saudi Arabia's western region contains key energy infrastructure including the Yanbu terminal, a major facility for crude oil exports, and the Jazan refinery in the far southwest of the country bordering Yemen.
Houthi fighters have attacked these major oil installations in recent weeks, alongside strikes on airports and military sites.
Saudi Arabia, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government against the Houthis, is the world's largest crude exporter.
Houthi attacks have killed 26 people in Saudi Arabia since September, including 23 in strikes on airports, according to the kingdom's authorities.

On Thursday (November 19), a tower housing the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund in Riyadh's financial district sustained damage on several floors in a Houthi attack, authorities said.
A skyscraper belonging to state oil giant Aramco was also damaged in a strike at the beginning of the month.

As far as trailblazers go, Kadambini Ganguly will figure right on top of several lists. She was a pioneering woman physician, the first to practice successfully in India, a gynaecologist and a social reformer who, equally efficiently, managed a large family as well. The story of Kadambini Ganguly is one of extraordinary achievement, and if told widely, will continue to inspire the young women of today.

In a profile published in Cureus in 2024, the authors point to the influence of the progressive Bramho Samaj movement, initiated by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, that helped Kadambini emerge from the shackles of conservative orthodoxy that might have stiffled her immense talent. “This environment, which championed the values of education and gender equality, contributed significantly to shaping her exemplary career and lifelong dedication to social justice,” the article reads. Records of her life acknowledge that she was partly recognised during her lifetime, but also mercilessly criticised and defamed for being a progressive, working woman. The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades.

articles.title: In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare. Poverty, land alienation, and the erosion of traditional food systems, are taking a toll on maternal and child health in this predominantly tribal region of Keralam

Between the pages of a logbook recording Dakshina’s treatment are ₹100, ₹50, ₹20, and ₹10 notes. Dakshina’s mother, Minnal Rani, had filed them away for her daughter’s medical expenses. The child is gone, but the money remains untouched. “We will never spend it,” she says, fighting back tears.

Dakshina was five months old when doctors detected a hole in her heart. Born on June 13, 2025, she was taken to many hospitals, including one in Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam’s capital. With surgery ruled out, she was eventually referred to a cooperative hospital at Perinthalmanna, in Malappuram district, a two-and-a-half-hour drive away from home. She died here, on April 13, 2026.
Rani and her husband Chandra Sekhar say the hospital refused to release their daughter’s body until they paid a bill of ₹10,000. They managed to raise the money with the help of a ward councillor.
“We buried her under that tree,” says Rani, pointing to a coconut tree near their house at Vechapathi hamlet in Sholayur panchayat of Attappadi, Palakkad district.

Dakshina’s death is among a series of 10 infant deaths reported this year from Attappadi, a predominantly tribal settlement. There have been four back-to-back deaths in October. Of the 10 infant deaths, six involved congenital anomalies, with heart defects among the commonly reported conditions. An expert committee of doctors and researchers is examining the deaths.

articles.title: Congress proposes four-point formula for delimitation, says INDIA bloc on board
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Party proposes retaining 543 Lok Sabha seats, existing State-wise distribution and a 25-year freeze, with one-third reservation for women

The Congress party on Friday said it favoured resolving the issue of delimitation through consultations with all political parties, but accused the government of making no effort to engage the Opposition on the matter.

Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said the party’s position was guided by a four-point formula: retaining the existing strength of 543 seats in the Lok Sabha; maintaining the present State-wise distribution of seats; reserving one-third (182) of the existing seats for women; and imposing a 25-year freeze on all three arrangements.

Mr. Ramesh said the need for an early consensus on the issue had become more pressing in view of of the fact that Article 82 of the Constitution will come into force and delimitation would be held once the results of the ongoing Census exercise are out early next year.
This could be unfavourable to some southern states – which have made progress in population control – and hence not feasible, he added.
Mr. Ramesh said the Congress was not opposed to delimitation as such, but believed that the exercise should not place any State at a disadvantage.

The Congress leader claimed that all parties in the INDIA bloc, including the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and the Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar), were on the same page on the four-point formula.
The DMK, he said, was also party to a resolution opposing any change in the number of Lok Sabha seats and seeking safeguards to ensure that Tamil Nadu was not disadvantaged by delimitation.
The Congress leader said seeking consultation was necessary because the government had not initiated any meaningful engagement with the Opposition.
He claimed that as per his information, the government has not shared a concrete proposal on delimitation even with constituents of the National Democratic Alliance.
The Congress wanted the matter to be discussed with all political parties and stakeholders to arrive at a consensus, Mr. Ramesh added.
The Monsoon session of Parliament has remained unprorogued since both Houses were adjourned sine die on August 13.

The decision has fuelled speculation about the possibility of the government convening Parliament at short notice to consider the proposed constitutional changes linked to women’s reservation and delimitation.

articles.title: Woman delivers triplets after non-ART treatment at Telangana govt. hospital; premature babies discharged after NICU care
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: After a nine-year wait and unsuccessful fertility treatment at private hospitals, a couple welcomed triplet boys following treatment at Gandhi Hospital’s IVF Centre. The premature babies, who weighed between 1.4 kg and 1.5 kg at birth, spent over a month in the hospital’s Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU). They were discharged along with their 32-year-old mother after responding well to treatment.
Avanthi enrolled at Gandhi Hospital’s IVF Centre in January this year. Doctors opted for ovulation induction, a non-assisted reproductive treatment, and she conceived in the second cycle.

After scans revealed a triplet pregnancy and a short cervix, doctors performed a McDonald’s cervical cerclage at 14 weeks. However, her water broke prematurely at 32 weeks, prompting doctors to deliver the babies on October 7. The newborns were admitted to the NICU, where they received treatment and close monitoring for over a month before being discharged with their mother.

Director of Medical Education Vanii appreciated the efforts of the team, including head of the Department of Gynaecology Shobha, IVF specialists Krishnaveni and Fathima Rafi, embryologist Shiva Krishna, lab technician Ashok and counsellor Kavitha.

IVF specialist Dr Krishnaveni said that they opted ovulation induction as a first line of treatment, which is not a In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) method. “We conduct evaluations to know if non-IVF methods can be used as first line of treatment to avoid burden on couples who are already in distress,” she said. Currently, over 500 couples have rolled for treatments at the government hospitals IVF centre.

articles.title: IJCCI to lead business delegation to Japan from Nov. 30
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Indo-Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry (IJCCI) organised a business networking meeting with a 16-member business delegation from Osaka, Japan, to strengthen bilateral business ties and explore opportunities for trade, investment, and industrial collaboration between India and Japan.
The delegation was led by Hiromitsu Morishima, Chairperson, International Business Committee, Osaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry, and Yasushi Ninomiya, Director-General, JETRO Osaka.
The companies spoke about their products and business opportunities.
To strengthen bilateral economic relations, IJCCI is leading a 16-member delegation to Japan from November 30 to December 4.
The delegation will visit Tokyo, Yokohama, Kochi, Fukuoka, Hiroshima, and Osaka.
“We particularly look forward to strengthening our engagement with Osaka, which is one of Japan’s leading commercial and industrial centres,” said IJCCI president S. Padmanabhan.
“India, with its large domestic market, growing manufacturing capabilities, and developing digital economy, offers significant opportunities for Japanese businesses,” Mr. Padmanabhan added.
He further said that Indian companies can benefit from Japanese technology, management practices, and innovation.

articles.title: Infra push and low base effect pushes core sector growth to series-high of 10.9% in October 2026
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: While the coal and electricity sectors saw growth shoot up, a large part of this was due to a statistical effect rather than growth in actual output. On the other hand, fuel-related sectors contracted again

Growth in the core industrial sectors of the economy climbed to a series-high of 10.9% in October 2026, driven by a surge in electricity generation, and coal, cement, and iron ore production, and a low base effect, official data released on Friday (November 20, 2026) showed.

Data released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry on the Index of Core Industries shows that growth in October surpassed the 8.2% in September, the previous series high. The new index, released this year with a base year of 2022-23, has data that goes back only up to April 2024.
However, the data also shows that the strong growth figure in October was also likely aided by the fact that the index grew a relatively poor 0.8% in October last year.

“While core output surged by 10.9% in October 2026, the fastest pace in the new series, this was supported by a low base related to the shift in the festive calendar, with output having expanded by a marginal 0.8% in the year ago month,” Aditi Nayar, chief economist at ICRA said.

“While the growth print for October 2026 signals a strong start for the third quarter of FY2027, this is largely optical,” Ms. Nayar added. “The average performance for October-November 2026 would provide a better assessment, as this would adjust for festive base effects.”

Within the index, the coal sector saw growth accelerating to 23.05% in October 2026, far faster than the 10.7% registered in September. October’s performance, however, is likely also due to low base effect, since the sector contracted 8.4% in October last year.

The growth in the index, however, is in line with what the industry itself has reported. Coal India, the country’s largest coal company, reported that production increased about 19% to 67.2 million tonnes (MT) in October.

A major reason for the growth in coal production was likely demand from the power sector, which saw electricity generation jump by 21.6% in October 2026, up from 12.6% in the previous month. However, this sector too could have benefited from a low base effect, since it contracted nearly 7% in October 2025.
Within the index, the infrastructure-related sectors were the only ones that grew strongly without the aid of a statistical low base effect.

The iron ore sector, for example, grew at a three-month high of 23.4% in October 2026, compared to 18.4% in September and 8.7% in October last year. One of the factors driving this strong growth was that steel production grew at 7.3% in October, the fastest rate in seven months.
The cement sector also grew at a series-high of 15.4% in October 2026, compared to 10.1% in September, and 5.2% in October last year.
The fuel-related sectors in the Index other than coal continued to perform relatively poorly.

articles.title: Following Cyclone Akvan, monsoon rain to resume over T.N. from tomorrow
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The RMC has forecast moderate rainfall in coastal districts, including Chennai and Cuddalore, and mild rainfall over adjoining areas; wet weather likely to last till the first week of December

Following Cyclone Akvan’s passage on Friday morning, most parts of Tamil Nadu are likely to experience a brief break in monsoon activity, accompanied by a dip in night-time temperatures. Wet weather is expected to return on Sunday and intensify over the subsequent days.
The break in rainfall is expected to raise day temperatures by two or three degrees Celsius in a few pockets of the State.
The Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) has also forecast ground frost at isolated places in the Nilgiris and Kodaikanal till Sunday.

The absence of widespread rainfall has pushed various districts, including Tiruvarur, Thanjavur, Madurai, Salem, and Chengalpattu, into the rainfall deficit category. The State has so far received nearly 26 cm of monsoon rainfall, which is 14% lower than its seasonal share since October 1.
RMC officials said Cyclone Akvan was expected to weaken into a depression on Friday, and gradually fade away.

V.R. Durai, Head, Regional Weather Forecasting Centre, RMC, said dry and cold northwesterly winds and the absence of cloud cover and rainfall led to a rise in day temperatures and drop in minimum temperatures over most parts of the State.

A trough in the easterly wave is likely to revive rainfall activity from Sunday and bring intense rainfall from Monday as it moves across the State. While coastal districts are expected to benefit more, interior Tamil Nadu is also likely to receive moderate rainfall till November 26.
“We are expecting wet weather in the State till December first week, with a low pressure area likely to form then. The sustained rainfall activity may narrow rainfall deficit,” he said.
The RMC has forecast moderate rainfall over coastal districts, including Chennai, Cuddalore, and Nagapattinam, on Sunday and mild rainfall over areas adjoining coastal districts.
On Monday, rainfall is expected to intensify over 10 coastal districts, including Cuddalore, Thoothukudi, and Kanniyakumari.
While the wet spell would cover the entire State, intensity of rainfall would vary. For instance, districts such as Chennai, Ranipet, Villupuram, and Karur would receive moderate rainfall.

For November 24, the RMC has issued yellow alert to coastal districts from Tiruvallur to Kanniyakumari, indicating heavy rainfall, with wind speeds of up to 50 kmph. Interior and Western Ghats districts are expected to receive moderate rainfall.

articles.title: Anthropic researcher says Claude solved maths’ greatest riddle
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics

A mathematician at AI company Anthropic said Friday (November 20, 2026) that he had used the firm’s Claude chatbot to prove the Riemann Hypothesis, a problem that has eluded mathematicians for more than 160 years.
“I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Levent Alpoge wrote in a four-page note released Friday (November 20, 2026).
The claim has not been independently verified, and the proof has not yet been reviewed by outside experts.

First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics.
It is one of seven Millennium Prize Problems selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute in 2000, which offers $1 million for a solution to each.
Under the institute’s rules, a solution must be published in a peer-reviewed journal and withstand two years of scrutiny.
Mr. Alpoge said the method also resolves a broader version of the problem known as the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis.

He said he and Claude had produced a version of the proof in Lean, a programming language that allows mathematical arguments to be checked by a computer, and that he was releasing only that version for now.
A full written argument would be extremely long, he said, adding that he had not yet mastered all of the mathematics involved and planned to write it up properly.

Mr. Alpoge said he had consulted Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei before announcing the result and acknowledged that its timing could be viewed cynically, without elaborating, though he was probably referring to this week’s record IPO.
In August, Anthropic said an unreleased version of Claude had improved a long-standing result related to the Riemann Hypothesis, while stressing that it had not proved it.
Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment from AFP.

articles.title: West Bengal CEO office postpones SSR due to unavoidable circumstances
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The development comes ahead of pending civic elections in West Bengal. The State government is keen to hold elections to the civic bodies of Howrah and Kolkata.

The West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer’s (CEO) office announced on Friday (November 20, 2026) the postponement of the Special Summary Revision (SSR) of the Photo Electoral Roll, 2027, which was scheduled to commence on November 23. The CEO’s office, in a statement, added that the decision has been taken due to “unavoidable circumstances.” The revised schedule for the exercise will be intimated subsequently, the statement said.
Editorial | Incomplete remedies: On Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls

“The upcoming programme of Special Summary Revision of Photo Electoral Roll, which was scheduled from 23 November 2026 onwards, is hereby postponed due to some unavoidable circumstances,” the press statement said. As per the SSR schedule announced in the State, the publication of final electoral rolls is scheduled for January 2027.

The SSR, an annual exercise, usually seeks to enrol eligible voters—particularly young and first-time electors—and facilitate advance applications from those who will become eligible on April 1, July 1, and October 1, 2027. However, it had not been carried out after the SIR was launched last year.

The development comes ahead of pending civic elections in West Bengal. The state government is keen to hold elections to the civic bodies of Howrah and Kolkata. The Calcutta High Court had stayed elections to the Kolkata Municipal Corporation on the grounds that the challenge to the delimitation of wards of the civic body should be addressed by the Court before elections are declared.

The SSR will not come to the aid of the 38 lakh electors whose fate is pending before SIR tribunals after their names were removed from the voter list. According to an affidavit filed by the ECI in September earlier this year, of the 27 lakh electors who were excluded from the electoral rolls on the ground of “logical discrepancies,” 22 lakh voters have filed appeals before the tribunal challenging their exclusion. The EC’s affidavit also added that 16.10 lakh appeals have been filed against inclusions during SIR. This puts the total number of appeals of 38 lakh electors pending before the SIR tribunals.

articles.title: Patna High Court quashes dismissal of teachers and staff of Sanskrit Colleges
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The court has directed the Bihar Education Department to release the grant-in-aid to the university within three months.

Principals, teachers, and non-teaching staff of various Sanskrit colleges affiliated with Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (KSDSU) received relief from the Patna High Court on Friday (November 20, 2026).

A single-judge bench presided over by Justice Kumar Manish, while hearing 12 connected petitions (lead case: Birendra Prasad Thakur v. State of Bihar, CWJC No. 13475/2022), quashed all dismissal orders issued by the Director of Higher Education and the university.

The petitioners were appointed between 2008 and 2015 in various affiliated and “deficit grant-in-aid” Sanskrit colleges located in Supaul, West Champaran, East Champaran, Patna, Saran, and Jehanabad, following due process involving public advertisements and selection committees.

Despite the university’s Syndicate confirming their services, the Director of Higher Education cited the absence of prior approval from the State Government, as required under Section 35(2) of the Bihar State Universities Act, 1976, and rejected these appointments on April 21, 2022, and November 2, 2022. Subsequently, the university issued directives to terminate their services.

In its judgment, the High Court cited the ruling of a Full Bench in Braj Kishore Singh v. State of Bihar (1997). The Court clarified that, when posts have already been created and sanctioned (under an established ‘staffing pattern’) pursuant to the State Government’s resolution dated October 18, 1976, separate ‘prior approval’ from the government is not mandatory for appointments to those posts made through a valid selection process.
“Dismissing an employee on technical grounds after more than a decade of service constitutes a violation of Articles 14, 16, and 21 of the Constitution,” the court observed.
Expressing concern over the proliferation of unnecessary litigation in cases of a similar nature, the court cited Clause 4(C)(1) of the Bihar State Litigation Policy, 2011.
The court directed that a copy of the order be sent to the Chief Secretary and the Advocate General. The court emphasised that such similar cases should be resolved at the departmental level.

Declaring the service of all the petitioners to be valid, the court has directed the Bihar Education Department to release the grant-in-aid to the university within three months of receiving a copy of the order.
“This is to ensure that the petitioners receive their regular current salaries, as well as all outstanding salary arrears accrued from the date of their initial appointment,” the court said.

articles.title: Transgender persons to be roped in for tax collection in West Bengal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: West Bengal Minister Agnimitra Paul launches a programme to provide dignified, alternative livelihoods to trans persons

The West Bengal government will engage transgender persons to collect municipal tax and spread traffic awareness. Urban Development and Municipal Affairs Minister Agnimitra Paul said the initiative, called “Brihannala Brigade”, will provide an opportunity for a dignified livelihood for the transpersons.

“The CM wishes that they (transgender people no) longer have to resort to begging at traffic signals; instead, we want to offer them an alternative, respectable livelihood. We have decided that those among them who are interested will receive training from the police and be deployed at traffic signals. Their role will be to sensitise the public about traffic rules and safety measures,” Ms. Paul said on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

She further added that another group of transgender persons would be trained to collect outstanding taxes, which could help address the staff shortage that leads to delayed collections and large pending amounts.

The Minister also added that each of these transgender individuals will be provided with training to engage in this work so that they can conduct better public interaction and do their work seamlessly. They will receive a stipend for the work, Ms. Paul said.

The West Bengal government has started an initiative to offer relief in paying outstanding property taxes, including in the actual sums and interest, to encourage defaulters to pay their outstanding balances.
According to Kolkata Municipal Corporation estimates, they have around ₹6800 crore outstanding property tax pending, including personal properties, mixed-use properties, and commercial properties.

In 2022, the previous Mamata Banerjee government decided to allow transgender persons to apply for government jobs under the general category to help them have better opportunities in employment. A Transgender Development Board was set up in 2017, but the board could not undertake many activities for the welfare of members of the community. The last census carried out in the state in 2011 put the number of transgender people in the state at 30,349. The actual number of people of the third gender may be higher, several groups working for the community say.

articles.title: Trinamool supporters attacked outside the police station as police questioned Abhishek
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The supporters of Trinamool had gathered outside the police station in support of Abhishek Banerjee

Supporters of Mamata All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) were allegedly attacked on Friday (November 20, 2026) by supporters of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) outside a police station while party leader Abhishek Banerjee was being questioned by Kolkata Police at the Girish Park police station.

Videos of the scuffle and the assault on women supporters of the Trinamool were shared on social media and by the Mamata AITC. In the videos, groups of women alleged to be BJP supporters were seen chasing another group of women. Supporters of the Trinamool had gathered outside the police station in support of Abhishek Banerjee. The BJP leaders denied allegations of the assault but claimed that Trinamool supporters were trying to incite tensions by gathering outside the police station.

“@BJP4Bengal workers gathered outside Girish Park Police Station today, seemingly intent on harassing, heckling and assaulting our workers, did not even spare ordinary citizens and parents who had come to pick up their children from school,” the party shared on social media. The Mamata AITC leader raised questions on the role of politics.

The police complaint against the Diamond Harbour MP was filed in connection with remarks reportedly made by him on 29 October, in which he criticised sections of the police administration, alleging that officers were acting under political pressure. Mr. Banerjee took to social media to share videos of BJP leaders, including Suvendu Adhikari, alleging threats to the police when they were in the Opposition.

After the BJP came to power, several FIRs were registered against Abhishek Banerjee. He has been summoned to appear before the police on numerous occasions. Later in the day, the Trinamool leader filed a Zero FIR at Girish Park Police Station, highlighting how Suvendu Adhikari, Dilip Ghosh, and other BJP leaders threatened the Kolkata Police and the West Bengal Police on multiple occasions.

“The expertise and urgency shown by Girish Park PS in connection with Abhishek Banerjee’s matter—we hope the same expertise and urgency will be shown by them in connection with this Zero FIR, and that they will investigate the matter,” Arka Nag, an advocate representing Trinamool Congress leader, said.

articles.title: Chandel district official issues advisory after spurious liquor kills 11 in Manipur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Chandel district authorities have urged the people to report suspected manufacturing, storage, sale or distribution of adulterated liquor
Manipur’s Chandel district administration on Friday (November 20, 2026) issued an advisory, urging people to report suspected manufacturing, storage, sale or distribution of adulterated liquor.
The public advisory followed the death of 11 people due to consumption of spurious liquor in the district’s Chakpikarong Sub-Division. The deaths have been reported since Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

According to a statement from the Chief Minister’s Office, 180 others are undergoing treatment at two private hospitals in Imphal. Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited these hospitals on Friday and took stock of the treatment being provided to the patients.

Advising the general public to exercise utmost caution, the district administration said the cause of the deaths was yet to be “medically and scientifically established”. It asked people to refrain from consuming locally brewed liquor or alcoholic beverages of doubtful origin, particularly from suspected sources in the affected areas.

“Any person experiencing vomiting, abdominal pain, headache, dizziness, blurred vision, breathing difficulty or other unusual symptoms following alcohol consumption should immediately seek medical attention at the nearest facility,” the advisory read.
It also advised people who may have consumed liquor from the same suspected source to seek medical evaluation even if they are not experiencing symptoms.

“The public is requested to report suspected manufacturing, storage, sale or distribution of adulterated liquor to the nearest police station or the concerned authorities,” the advisory further read, requesting village authorities, civil society organisations, women’s organisations and youth clubs to assist in spreading awareness.

The Manipur government partially lifted 30 years of alcohol prohibition in December 2023, although extremist groups in the State continue to target liquor businesses. Years of prohibition led to certain areas turning into local liquor dens, selling alcoholic beverages of suspect quality.
Spurious liquor has claimed lives in other northeastern States where prohibition is enforced. For instance, 23 people were killed in Nagaland’s Mokokchung and Tuensang districts about two months ago.

articles.title: PM to visit Bihar to inaugurate a six-lane bridge named after ex-CM Nitish
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: JD(U) working chief Sanjay Kumar Jha said that “the decision of CM Choudhary to name the bridge as Nitish Setu symbolises the immense affection, respect, and gratitude that Bihar people have for our leader Nitish Kumar”

On the completion of one year of NDA government rule in Bihar, Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit the Vaishali district on November 21 to inaugurate a six-lane bridge and lay the foundation stone for several other projects. PM Modi is also likely to address a public meeting after the scheduled ceremonies in the district.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to inaugurate a 9.76 km long ₹5,500 crore six-lane bridge on the River Ganga, connecting Kacchi Dargah in Patna district to Bidupur in the neighbouring Vaishali district. The government has named the bridge after former Chief Minister and ruling NDA ally Nitish Kumar as “Nitish Setu.”

The Opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal recently raised objections, claiming that the bridge was conceived in 2015 when the Mahagathbandhan (grand alliance) government was in power in the State, and the party has also demanded that the bridge be named after RJD chief Lalu Prasad.

RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav, who is also the leader of the Opposition in the State Assembly, and his parents Lalu Prasad and Rabri Devi, have been representing the flood-prone Raghopur for several terms in the Assembly and the constituency has been a bastion of the Other Backward Class “Yadav” caste for long.

“Nitish Setu will make travel between north and south Bihar smoother and faster, offering significant benefits to the people of Patna, Vaishali, and surrounding districts,” Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary said. However, RJD national working president Tejashwi Yadav took a dig at this, expressing wonder: “I’ve heard that such bridges or monuments are only named after people who are no more. I guess the BJP, by naming the bridge as Nitish Setu, has gobbled up Nitish Kumar, and he doesn’t exist for them.”

However, JD(U) working president Sanjay Kumar Jha said that “the decision of Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary to name the bridge as Nitish Setu symbolises the immense affection, respect, and gratitude that the people of Bihar have for our leader Nitish Kumar ji.”

For the first time in the state, senior BJP leader Samrat Choudhary became Chief Minister in April 2026, replacing the ruling alliance leader of JD(U), Nitish Kumar. Mr. Kumar’s son, Nishant Kumar, is the Health Minister in Mr. Choudhary’s cabinet. Following in the footsteps of his predecessor and former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary is likely to embark on his statewide tour on November 26, 2026, from the West Champaran district.

Meanwhile, BJP sources in Bihar said that Union Home Minister and senior party leader Amit Shah might visit Bihar next month, though “the place and exact date of his visit have not been confirmed yet”.

articles.title: Three to tango: On Trump, Xi, Putin trilateral summit
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: U.S., China, Russia must draw up a roadmap for talks on nuclear weapons

The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.

Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: Why a shortage of clinical psychologists in Keralam govt hospitals is leaving people with intellectual disabilities waiting for certificates
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: As per the last Kerala Disability Census in 2015, there are about 80,000 persons with various intellectual challenges. However, government hospitals and medical college hospitals in the State currently have only 22 clinical psychologists to conduct IQ assessment tests

People with intellectual disabilities in Keralam are struggling to obtain and renew disability certificates due to a severe shortage of clinical psychologists in government hospitals to conduct Intelligence Quotient (IQ) assessment tests.

As per the latest disability assessment guidelines issued by the Union government’s Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, differently-abled children must undergo assessment tests at least thrice before they turn 18 to obtain permanent disability certificates. During all these assessment phases, an IQ test is a must. However, there are only 22 clinical psychologists under the Directorate of Health Services (DHS) and the Directorate of Medical Education (DME) put together – 17 under the DHS and the rest under the DME.

National & Polity Report: Why a shortage of clinical psychologists in Keralam govt hospitals is leaving people with intellectual disabilities waiting for certificates. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and administrative governance framework.

Institutional Framework: The update directly connects with parliamentary procedures, centre-state relations under the Seventh Schedule, and constitutional bodies responsible for upholding statutory mandates.

articles.title: In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare. Poverty, land alienation, and the erosion of traditional food systems, are taking a toll on maternal and child health in this predominantly tribal region of Keralam

Between the pages of a logbook recording Dakshina’s treatment are ₹100, ₹50, ₹20, and ₹10 notes. Dakshina’s mother, Minnal Rani, had filed them away for her daughter’s medical expenses. The child is gone, but the money remains untouched. “We will never spend it,” she says, fighting back tears.

Dakshina was five months old when doctors detected a hole in her heart. Born on June 13, 2025, she was taken to many hospitals, including one in Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam’s capital. With surgery ruled out, she was eventually referred to a cooperative hospital at Perinthalmanna, in Malappuram district, a two-and-a-half-hour drive away from home. She died here, on April 13, 2026.
Rani and her husband Chandra Sekhar say the hospital refused to release their daughter’s body until they paid a bill of ₹10,000. They managed to raise the money with the help of a ward councillor.
“We buried her under that tree,” says Rani, pointing to a coconut tree near their house at Vechapathi hamlet in Sholayur panchayat of Attappadi, Palakkad district.

Dakshina’s death is among a series of 10 infant deaths reported this year from Attappadi, a predominantly tribal settlement. There have been four back-to-back deaths in October. Of the 10 infant deaths, six involved congenital anomalies, with heart defects among the commonly reported conditions. An expert committee of doctors and researchers is examining the deaths.

articles.title: PDP’s Iltija, CPI(M)’s Tarigami express concern over ‘rising scams’ in government-run recruiting agencies in J&K
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Hitting out at J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, Iltija Mufti said, The latest controversy has once again exposed serious concerns surrounding the conduct of recruitment examinations in J&K

People’s Democratic Party (PDP) leader Iltija Mufti and CPI(M) legislator M.Y. Tarigami on Friday (November 20, 2026) flagged the recent cheating racket in the Finance Accounts Assistant (FAA) recruitment examination, with Ms. Mufti demanding “cancellation or postponement of upcoming recruitment examinations until an impartial investigation establishes the extent of the cheating racket”.

“The seizure of four modules, eight wireless devices, 22 mobile phones and four vehicles in connection with the alleged racket raised serious questions about the examination process and the functioning of the recruitment authorities. It’s not a one-off incident but a pattern since 2019. It is a mafia and a proper syndicate operating with the collusion and assistance of government employees,” said Ms. Mufti.

Hitting out at J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah , Ms. Mufti said, “The latest controversy has once again exposed serious concerns surrounding the conduct of recruitment examinations in J&K. Repeated cancellations, allegations of malpractice and assurances that remain unfulfilled have left thousands of aspirants paying the price. Our youth deserve a transparent, credible and accountable recruitment system, not another round of committees and hollow promises.”

On November 16, the J&K Police busted a cheating module in Jammu and arrested locals allegedly using mobile and wireless devices during the J&K Service Selection Board (JKSSB) examination for the posts of Finance Assistants. Nearly 1.62 lakh aspirants had appeared for around 600 posts across J&K in the examination.

“The recruitment examinations conducted since 2019 have repeatedly faced allegations of paper leaks, cheating and irregularities, like the Police Sub-Inspector recruitment examination in 2021 and irregularities in Jal Shakti. This time, officials associated with the JKSSB and the Forest Department had also come under the scanner of the investigating agencies,” said Ms. Mufti.

Citing the recent review meeting of Mr. Abdullah regarding recruitment processes, Ms. Mufti said, “the JKSSB is a mafia, not a board. Around ₹113 crore collected in application fees, repeated recruitment scams, paper leaks and thousands of shattered dreams. When credit comes, JKSSB is yours (Mr. Abdullah), when scams happen, it’s not?”

She also demanded publication of the sub-committee report on rationalisation of reservations in J&K, alleging that the issue had remained pending for nearly two years despite concerns raised by open-merit candidates.

CPI(M)‘s Tarigami also expressed concern over the latest cheating scam in Jammu. “Repeated recruitment irregularities and paper leaks have eroded the confidence of J&K‘s youth in the selection system. The latest addition to a series of recruitment scams and examination-related irregularities is the FAA examination. The incident has raised serious questions about the security of examinations, possible insider involvement and institutional accountability,” said Mr. Tarigami.

He said thousands of aspirants invest years of hard work, family savings and personal sacrifices to secure public jobs. “They deserve a fair, transparent and merit-based system, not one that repeatedly puts their aspirations at risk,” he said.

Mr. Tarigami said the future of an entire generation could not be held hostage to institutional failures and stressed the need for transparency and accountability in the recruitment process. “Restoring the confidence of job aspirants requires ensuring a credible, impartial and merit-based selection mechanism,” he added.

articles.title: What is the controversy over the relocation of the Central Secretariat Library? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Story So Far: The 135-year-old Central Secretariat Library in Delhi, which houses over 8.5 lakh books, is being shifted as part of the Central Vista redevelopment project. On September 17, the library, currently housed in the Shastri Bhawan complex, was directed to vacate the premises by September 30 as part of the redevelopment project. The Central Public Works Department (CPWD) had asked the library, along with other offices in the complex, to remove all furniture and electronic equipment ahead of demolition and reconstruction work. However, no clear space had been demarcated for the library.

Taking suo motu cognisance, the Supreme Court on October 5 sought a detailed affidavit from the Union government on the proposed relocation. Further, on November 20, the SC bench referred the matter to the Chief Justice of India so that an appropriate bench can be assigned.

articles.title: Heritage is not just Lutyens, but also books at the 135-year-old Central Secretariat Library, SC tells government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Centre says it values the books as a treasure; the library has tomes dating back to 1702

The Supreme Court on Friday (November 20, 2026) told the Union government that culture is not confined to preserving the Lutyens neighbourhood in the national capital but extends to protecting centuries’ old books of the 135-year-old Central Secretariat Library that are about to lose their home.

Appearing before a Bench headed by Justice Sanjay Kumar, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta and Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati agreed with the court that the books are a “treasure that we love”. The government repeated its November 16 undertaking to the court to not shift the book from its premises in Shastri Bhawan.”
“We are more concerned about the books. Heritage is not just the Lutyens... There are books dating back to 1702,” Justice Kumar expressed the court’s concern.
Mr. Mehta assured the court that the government was conscious of the weight of cultural value and heritage the books represent.

“The government will sit with the amicus curiae, senior advocate Haripriya Padmanabhan, and resolve the issue. Meanwhile, we stand by the undertaking given to the court on November 16,” Mr. Mehta assured.

Justice Kumar said the case was taken up by his Bench on a suo motu basis. However, his Bench did not have the public interest litigation (PIL) roster. The judge said the suo motu case would now be referred to the Chief Justice of India, who would allocate it to the appropriate Bench. Justice Kumar said it may likely come back to his Bench, but urged the government to hold true to its November 16 undertaking in the meanwhile.
The suo motu case was initiated on the basis of reports that the library was asked to vacate by September 30 as part of the redevelopment project.

On November 16, the court had observed its intention to examine the government’s proposal to permanently relocate the library to the under-construction Kartavya Bhawan-4 in Central Delhi as part of the Central Vista redevelopment project.
The Centre’s affidavit in the apex court had informed the court that space had been earmarked for both the Central Secretariat Library and the Tulsi Sadan Library in the proposed Kartavya Bhawan-4.

According to the affidavit, approximately 5,583 sq. m. has been allocated for the two libraries, comprising 4,112 sq. m. on the ground floor and 1,471 sq. m. on the first floor, compared with the 5,209.58 sq. m. they currently occupy. The government said the construction contract for Kartavya Bhawan-4 had been awarded and the building was scheduled for completion by December 2028.
Until then, books from the Central Secretariat Library were proposed to be shifted temporarily to the General Pool Office Accommodation complex in Netaji Nagar.
Ms. Padmanabhan, while narrating her visit to the facility where books from the Tulsi Sadan Library were stored, described the conditions as “atrocious”.
