The Supreme Court on Friday (November 20, 2026) told the Union government that culture is not confined to preserving the Lutyens neighbourhood in the national capital but extends to protecting centuries’ old books of the 135-year-old Central Secretariat Library that are about to lose their home.

Appearing before a Bench headed by Justice Sanjay Kumar, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta and Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati agreed with the court that the books are a “treasure that we love”. The government repeated its November 16 undertaking to the court to not shift the book from its premises in Shastri Bhawan.”

“We are more concerned about the books. Heritage is not just the Lutyens... There are books dating back to 1702,” Justice Kumar expressed the court’s concern.

Mr. Mehta assured the court that the government was conscious of the weight of cultural value and heritage the books represent.

“The government will sit with the amicus curiae, senior advocate Haripriya Padmanabhan, and resolve the issue. Meanwhile, we stand by the undertaking given to the court on November 16,” Mr. Mehta assured.

Justice Kumar said the case was taken up by his Bench on a suo motu basis. However, his Bench did not have the public interest litigation (PIL) roster. The judge said the suo motu case would now be referred to the Chief Justice of India, who would allocate it to the appropriate Bench. Justice Kumar said it may likely come back to his Bench, but urged the government to hold true to its November 16 undertaking in the meanwhile.

The suo motu case was initiated on the basis of reports that the library was asked to vacate by September 30 as part of the redevelopment project.

On November 16, the court had observed its intention to examine the government’s proposal to permanently relocate the library to the under-construction Kartavya Bhawan-4 in Central Delhi as part of the Central Vista redevelopment project.

The Centre’s affidavit in the apex court had informed the court that space had been earmarked for both the Central Secretariat Library and the Tulsi Sadan Library in the proposed Kartavya Bhawan-4.

According to the affidavit, approximately 5,583 sq. m. has been allocated for the two libraries, comprising 4,112 sq. m. on the ground floor and 1,471 sq. m. on the first floor, compared with the 5,209.58 sq. m. they currently occupy. The government said the construction contract for Kartavya Bhawan-4 had been awarded and the building was scheduled for completion by December 2028.

Until then, books from the Central Secretariat Library were proposed to be shifted temporarily to the General Pool Office Accommodation complex in Netaji Nagar.

Ms. Padmanabhan, while narrating her visit to the facility where books from the Tulsi Sadan Library were stored, described the conditions as “atrocious”.

articles.title: Russia dusts off its pre-war demands as the U.S. raises discussing European security at Ukraine talks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The proposal to discuss broader security arrangements for Europe was floated by Donald Trump’s envoys, and that has worried Ukraine and its Western allies, who fear it will play into Moscow’s hands and weaken NATO

After nearly five years of fighting in Ukraine, the Kremlin is eagerly embracing a U.S. offer to discuss post-war European security, and Moscow is using that diplomatic opening to reaffirm the tough demands that President Vladimir Putin put forward before the start of his full-scale invasion.

The proposal to discuss broader security arrangements for Europe was floated by U.S. President Donald Trump's envoys, and that has worried Ukraine and its Western allies, who fear it will play into Moscow's hands and weaken NATO.
The Kremlin strongly backed the U.S. idea, describing a review of the broader European security framework as vital for a settlement of Europe's most devastating conflict since World War II.

Mr. Putin discussed the Ukrainian conflict with Mr. Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, their first trilateral meeting . That encounter had fuelled fears in Ukraine that they could discuss a possible settlement without Kyiv's participation.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wants a ceasefire to include a security framework to ensure that Russia does not attack his country again, and European leaders argue that such an architecture already exists in the form of NATO.

In draft agreements submitted to the U.S. and NATO in December 2021, two months before the invasion, Russia demanded that Washington and its allies pledge to exclude NATO's expansion to Ukraine, Georgia or any other nation that was once part of the Soviet Union.
Moscow also demanded that the U.S. and its allies make a commitment to not deploy weapons or conduct any military activities in Ukraine and other ex-Soviet nations.
The documents also obliged the alliance not to station any troops in areas where they weren't present in 1997 — before NATO moved to incorporate former Soviet bloc countries and ex-Soviet republics.

They also suggested a freeze on patrols by Russian and U.S. warships and bombers near each other's borders. In addition, they called for efforts to reduce the risk of incidents involving Russia and NATO warships and aircraft, primarily in the Baltic and the Black seas; a reduction in the scope of military drills; and greater transparency and other confidence-building measures.
NATO allies have rejected the Russian demands as a nonstarter.

Mr. Putin described the West's refusal to consider these proposals as the main reason behind his decision to send troops into Ukraine on Feb. 24, 2022, arguing that he had to act to fend off a major threat to Russia's national security. Ukraine and its allies denounce the invasion as an unprovoked act of aggression.
Speaking after the meeting with the Chinese and U.S. Presidents, Mr. Putin reaffirmed his criticism of the West for failing to take Moscow's complaints about NATO's expansion into account.

articles.title: Key takeaways from the Quad, ASEAN-India, and East Asia Summits in Manila | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Apart from the bilateral visits, Mr. Modi’s multilateral ASEAN engagements showed a growing desire to work more closely with the grouping at a time when global powers are working in a more unilateral manner

Prime Minister Narendra Modi took part in three back-to-back multilateral meetings on the side-lines of the annual Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) summits in Manila this week. The summits, including the ASEAN-India Summit, East Asia Summit and then the Quad Summit along with U.S. President Donald Trump, Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi and Australian PM Anthony Alabanese ended with several concrete announcements. They also sent deeper underlying message on India’s broad-basing its ‘Act East’ and Indo-Pacific policies, even as the world turned its attention to the Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral later in the week.

In 2025, PM Modi had pulled out of attending the ASEAN Summits in Kuala Lumpur due to what was seen as a combination of domestic commitments around Diwali and trade friction with U.S. President Donald Trump. Ties with the Philippines have improved dramatically since President Bongbong Marcos’ visit to Delhi in August 2025, and hence it was doubly important for PM Modi to attend the two conferences hosted by him- the ASEAN- India summit, which includes Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste, and Vietnam, as well as the East Asia Summit, which brings in U.S., Russia, China, Japan and South Korea. In addition, the invitation to the Quad Summit hosted by the U.S. and being held for the first time in Mr. Trump’s turbulent presidency was important to fit in, given concerns over his commitment to the Indo-Pacific grouping, and PM Modi ended his day with that.

Global & Diplomatic Brief: Key takeaways from the Quad, ASEAN-India, and East Asia Summits in Manila | Explained. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and proactive engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

Geopolitical Significance: Strengthening strategic partnerships across the Indo-Pacific, Global South, and multilateral forums such as the UN, G20, BRICS, and SCO remains central to India's foreign policy.

articles.title: Iraq fire at Basra power station kills at least four, injures 30
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Civil defence ‌teams brought the fire at the Hartha ‌power station north of Basra ‌under ⁠control after firefighters responded ⁠to the incident, says Iraq’s state news agency
At least four people were killed ​and 30 injured in ‌a fire at a power ​station in southern Iraq ⁠on Saturday (November 21, 2026), with the toll expected to rise, security officials said.
Civil defence ‌teams brought the fire at the Hartha ‌power station north of Basra ‌under ⁠control after firefighters responded ⁠to the incident, Iraq’s state news agency, INA , reported.
The fire spread to neighbouring ​houses and ‌forced operations at the power station to stop, the security officials said.
The Hartha station ‌has an installed generating ​capacity of 800 megawatts but had been operating at ⁠around 400 megawatts before the fire, they said.
There was no ‌immediate official information on the cause of the fire or the extent of the damage, INA reported.

Iraq’s electricity infrastructure has long struggled ‌with decades of underinvestment, inadequate maintenance ​, and an inability to meet peak demand, particularly during ⁠the extremely hot summer months. Fires ⁠and technical failures at substations and power facilities have ‌previously disrupted electricity supplies and caused widespread outages.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The newly uncovered breaches at the FBI and USDA were described as hacks, which are different from outages like the ones that afflicted Microsoft Outlook and the Federal Aviation Administration

The FBI is investigating a ​suspected breach of a nationwide database ‌used by federal, state and ​local law enforcement agencies ⁠to share criminal justice information, CNN reported on Friday (November 20, 2026), citing two people ‌briefed on the investigation.

The apparent compromise of the National ‌Crime Information Center database would ‌mark ⁠the second intrusion involving ⁠an FBI system in recent months and the latest in a string ​of cyber incidents that ‌have alarmed U.S. officials over the past week.
The agency did not respond to a ‌request for comment from Reuters .
The ​FBI database is used by law enforcement agencies nationwide ⁠to store and share information on warrants, criminal histories and background ‌checks.
The U.S. Agriculture Department was also breached by hackers in cyberattacks, U.S. media reported on Friday.
It remains unclear whether these two incidents are related and who is responsible for them.
U.S. President Donald Trump has sought to calm the public and urged people to "relax", while officials said the various outages were not linked to criminal activity.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) told employees that a system used to facilitate payments to farmers was targeted in a cyberattack, NBC reported, citing two former USDA officials.
The hackers may use the payments system as a backdoor to access more sensitive material, the former officials told NBC.

The USDA deals with "a bunch of scary biologic issues" and "if an adversary or a competitor were to have access to that same information... they could use our own research against us," a former official was quoted as saying.

Previous high-profile cyber disruptions over the past week have included a global outage affecting hundreds of millions of Microsoft users and a nationwide halt ‌to air travel that disrupted more ​than 18,000 flights.

articles.title: Pakistan Climate Minister arrives in Delhi to attend SCO Civilisations Dialogue Forum
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Pakistan is the current chair of the SCO Council of Heads of State (CHS) (SCO_CHS) for the period of 2026-27; the event, which will be inaugurated by PM Modi, will be held at Delhi’s iconic Purana Quila (Old Fort), a 16th Century fort built by Emperor Humayun

Pakistan’s Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, Dr. Musadik Masood Malik , arrived in Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026) for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum, officials said.
Mr. Malik is representing Pakistan at a cultural meeting of the SCO in Delhi, the Pakistan High Commission in India said.
Pakistan is the current chair of the SCO Council of Heads of State (CHS) (SCO_CHS) for the period of 2026-27.

The SCO is represented by China, India, Russia, Iran, Pakistan, Belarus, and Central Asian countries such as Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, and Kazakhstan. Almost all the member countries of the SCO are ancient civilisations that date back to the BCE era.

The dialogue, which will be organised by the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of External Affairs, was proposed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the SCO leaders’ Summit in Tianjin last year and adopted by the SCO Council. According to the sources, the government has invited Pakistan’s Minister for National Heritage and Culture Aurungzeb Khan Khichi, for the event. Culture Ministers from the 10 member states, including China, Russia, Iran, Belarus and Central Asian states, 15 Dialogue partners and observer countries have been invited.

The event, which will be inaugurated by Mr. Modi, will be held at Delhi’s iconic Purana Quila (Old Fort), a 16th Century fort built by Emperor Humayun. The fort is also the site of many excavations showcasing India’s ancient past spanning nearly 3,000 years, from the Pre-Mauryan, Mauryan, Sunga, Kushana, Gupta, Post-Gupta period to medieval-era Rajput, Sultanate and Mughal periods, officials said, explaining its importance.

articles.title: ‘Look at India, they have low interest rates’: Trump says U.S. could achieve 14–15% economic growth
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: “In four days, I met more than 20 world leaders, secured two new trade deals, and about 10 others coming very soon,” Donald Trump told a press conference at the White House in Washington

U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday (November 20, 2026) said he secured two trade deals with Thailand and the Philippines during his visit to Manila, adding that around 10 more agreements were expected soon.
“In four days, I met more than 20 world leaders, secured two new trade deals, and about 10 others coming very soon,” Mr. Trump told a press conference at the White House in Washington.
ALSO WATCH APEC 2026: Key takeaways from remarks by Putin, Xi and other leaders
Mr. Trump also referred to India's interest rates and the high economic growth it achieved.

“Look at India, they have low interest rates, and they have a seven per cent growth rate,” Mr. Trump said, adding that the U.S. could achieve economic growth in the range of 14-15% if it had lower interest rates.
Mr Trump also referred to his meeting with the leaders of the Quad, comprising the U.S., India, Japan, and Australia.

"We announced the first-ever Quad Bureau Leaders' Forum to cooperate on matters of economic security, we launched a Quad SI Accelerator, and we agreed to a new collaboration on maritime security and surveillance operations" Mr. Trump said.
India and the U.S. finalised the framework for the first phase of the trade agreement in February. However, changes in the tariff landscape have led to further negotiations on the agreement.
India is seeking lower tariffs on its goods in the U.S. market than its competitors such as Bangladesh, Vietnam, and Cambodia.

articles.title: This 2D rhythm platformer video game is an ode to India’s multiplicities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Suri: The Seventh Note by Tathvamasi Studios is set in a universe controlled by evil music. The game was launched in October

The story of Suri: The Seventh Note, a 2D video game by Bengaluru-based Tathvamasi Studios, is set in a world corrupted by an evil version of music. Everything in this universe moves in tune with that nefarious sonic presence. The protagonist, Ajira, must find a fruit located at the centre of the island to save her mother from certain death. Soon, she realises her actions shall determine the fate of the island itself.

Suri: The Seventh Note is the brainchild of Glen Martin from Kochi, founder of Tathvamasi Studios, who is also the game director of the video. He is joined by Chitrak Srivastava, co-founder and the game’s art director. The game was launched on Playstation Store and Steam in October.

Glen, formerly a data scientist, found himself immersed in game-making during the pandemic. He began by making smaller games, with friends from different places joining him on a Discord server to help. “When we started to build the game, it was not meant to be a project. But once we realised its potential, we began to think about what could be unique about this game,” says Glen.
Glen Martin and Chitrak Srivastava | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

“At that point, I was playing a parry-focused combat game called Sekiro. It’s a very hard game, and I am not good at it. But then I saw a lot of streamers play the game skilfully, without even taking a single hit, and I realised that when the game is played at that level, it has a certain rhythmic quality to it,” he adds. “The sounds of the sword clinking, the jumps and movements, everything felt choreographed.”
This ultimately led him to turn Suri… into a rhythm platformer game.

Suri... is a mix of two different games: rhythm and platformer. Rhythm games are music-themed action games that assess a player’s sense of timing and metre, while platformers are a sub-genre where a main character moves through uneven terrain and suspended platforms.

“There are very few games that have done this before, so our well of references was limited. In Suri..., the world moves to the rhythm. All the things that you would normally interact with in a regular platformer, like traps, obstacles, etc., are all tied to the rhythm in our game. You have to listen to the music to understand when a thing would move up and down or when a leaf would open or close and so on,” explains Glen. “When played well, it feels like dancing through levels.”

In 2024, Suri was one of five games at the inaugural edition of PlayStation’s India Hero Project, an incubator programme from Sony Interactive Entertainment. This ultimately allowed Glen to quit his job and hire more people.
A still from Suri: The Seventh Note | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

One of the most intriguing aspects about Suri is the world it is set in. “Suri is set in our own version of mythical India. While we are inspired by Indian ethos and culture, we have not tried to mimic it or take things from it directly. We’ve tried to create our own world,” says Glen.

Chitrak says, “We wanted to create something that belongs to those places we grew up in. Usually when you play these games, they mostly have European or Japanese settings. We wanted to find something that we could relate to and have the world explore that side of our culture. That was the north star for us, while we began developing this world.”

articles.title: CCMB team identifies genes that spur nerve repair, raise possibility of paralysis treatment
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Scientists at the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB) , Hyderabad, have identified two genes that can restore damaged nerve cells’ ability to regenerate, raising the possibility of new gene-based treatments for paralysis caused by spinal cord injuries.

The study, led by Ishwariya Venkatesh, found that activating two developmental genes, NR2F1 and NR2F6, enabled severed nerve fibres to regrow across completely injured spinal cords in mice, leading to measurable improvements in movement.

The spinal cord transmits signals from the brain to the rest of the body, enabling movement and sensation. Damage to it can cause paralysis because nerve cells in adult mammals generally lose their ability to regenerate. Despite decades of research, there is no treatment that can restore the lost neural connections.

The researchers sought to understand why young neurons can grow and regenerate while adult neurons cannot. Their investigation focused on proteins that activate growth-related genes during development but become less active as the brain matures. articles.title: Over 1 crore HPV vaccines given to 14-year-old girls in nine months: Health Ministry
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Six States — Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Mizoram, Madhya Pradesh, and Bihar — have achieved 100% coverage of their identified target populations, the Ministry said

India has administered more than one crore doses of the HPV vaccine to 14-year-old girls under its national vaccination campaign in less than nine months, covering nearly 87% of the identified annual target, the Health Ministry said on Saturday (November 21, 2026).

The nationwide HPV vaccination campaign, launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in February this year, provides free, voluntary and single-dose vaccination to 14-year-old girls at designated government health facilities with parental consent.
The annual target cohort comprises around 1.2 crore girls, based on Registrar General of India (RGI) 2021 population estimates.
Six States — Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Mizoram, Madhya Pradesh, and Bihar — have achieved 100% coverage of their identified target populations, the Ministry said.
Among other States, Assam has recorded 95.63% coverage, followed by Telangana (95.28%), Karnataka (93.16%) and Uttarakhand (90.17%).
Chhattisgarh and Rajasthan have crossed the 80% mark with 86.21% and 85.23% coverage, respectively.
Kerala has recorded 77.02% coverage, Tamil Nadu 76.12%, Odisha 74.90% and the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu 72.99%.
In absolute numbers, Uttar Pradesh leads with more than 29.33 lakh girls vaccinated, followed by Bihar with over 13.70 lakh and Gujarat with more than 7.75 lakh, according to the Ministry.
The milestone reflects coordinated efforts by the Centre, States and Union Territories, district administrations, healthcare workers, teachers, parents and local communities, it said.

The campaign has also focused on community engagement and dissemination of science-based information on HPV vaccination, with healthcare professionals, including paediatricians, gynaecologists, and specialists from institutions such as AIIMS, helping address concerns about vaccine safety and effectiveness.

The U-WIN digital platform is being used for real-time monitoring, beneficiary tracking and digital vaccination records. It also enables parents to book vaccination slots and download digital certificates.
The Ministry said programme managers can use the platform to identify coverage gaps and eligible girls who are yet to be vaccinated, besides helping in planning and resource allocation.

articles.title: Pune startup develops atomic clock prototype amid growing export curbs on critical technologies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Atomic clocks are critical to satellite navigation, telecommunications, space missions and strategic systems, where highly precise and stable timekeeping is essential.

Amid growing export controls and restrictions on access to high-performance atomic clock technology, Pune-based deep-tech startup QuPrayog Private Limited has developed a laboratory-scale atomic clock prototype, marking a step towards India’s efforts to build indigenous capabilities in precision timing and quantum instrumentation.

The startup has developed a Rubidium-87 atomic clock using Coherent Population Trapping (CPT) technology in a seven-month development effort. Having achieved a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 4 prototype, the company is now working towards developing a miniature, integrated product before the end of 2027.

Atomic clocks are critical to satellite navigation, telecommunications, space missions and strategic systems, where highly precise and stable timekeeping is essential. However, international export controls on dual-use technologies have made access to advanced atomic clocks challenging, highlighting the need for domestic alternatives and a reliable indigenous supply chain.

According to the company's experimental measurements, the prototype has demonstrated significant improvements in timekeeping stability, performing nearly 50 times better than a conventional free-running crystal oscillator over a period of 1,000 seconds, the company said in a press release.

Explaining the significance of the development, Dr Jay Mangaonkar, CEO and co-founder of QuPrayog, said, “Our objective is to reduce India’s dependence on imported atomic clocks and establish a reliable domestic supply chain for high-performance timing systems developed and manufactured in India. We want these critical technologies to be accessible to Indian companies building the next generation of navigation, space and strategic systems.”

As part of India’s push towards self-reliance and its Viksit Bharat 2047 vision, the Centre launched the National Quantum Mission in 2023, with an allocation of ₹6,003.65 crore over eight years. The mission aims to develop indigenous capabilities in quantum technologies, including sensing, metrology and precision measurement.

articles.title: Earthshot Prize finalists offer climate solutions for Mumbai, from wildfire detection to coastal protection and heat resilience
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: María Buhigas, Chief City Architect of Barcelona, said coastal cities such as Mumbai must reconsider traditional infrastructure-led approaches to protecting waterfronts against rising sea levels, intense rainfall and increasingly powerful waves

From using artificial intelligence to detect wildfires, redesigning coastlines to withstand increasingly violent storms and protecting vulnerable communities from extreme heat, three finalists of the 2026 Earthshot Prize have outlined climate solutions that could be adapted to Indian cities, including Mumbai.

Speaking in separate interviews on the sidelines of the Earthshot Prize Awards in Mumbai, representatives of Satellites on Fire, Barcelona’s Coastal Resilience Initiative and the Mahila Housing Trust discussed their approaches to tackling climate-related challenges and the opportunities for expanding their work in India.

Franco Rodríguez Viau, the 23-year-old CEO and co-founder of Argentina-based Satellites on Fire, said his organisation was looking to enter India through partnerships with government agencies, forestry companies and other stakeholders.
Founded in 2020 when Mr. Viau was 16, the company developed an AI-powered system that analyses imagery from 13 satellites every five minutes to identify heat signatures associated with wildfires.
“Our AI is able to detect fires, on average, 35 minutes faster than NASA’s system,” he said, adding that the platform identifies around 30% more fires than NASA’s system.

The technology combines satellite imagery with weather conditions, vegetation data and topography to identify fires and predict how they could spread over the following hours. Alerts are sent directly to firefighters and forest authorities through WhatsApp or SMS, accompanied by Google Maps locations and projections of the fire’s spread.
Mr. Viau said the platform currently operates in 21 countries across five continents and assists in responding to more than 2,000 wildfires annually.

Citing an incident at a national park in Argentina, he said the system detected a wildfire 17 minutes after it began, nearly two hours before NASA’s system registered it. The early warning, he said, enabled firefighting teams to respond before the blaze reached nearby homes.
On expanding to India, Mr. Viau said the technology required no additional hardware installation and could be deployed once local partnerships were established.
“We can start monitoring India from one day to the other. The only thing that we need is connections here,” he said, adding that the company was open to joint ventures and partnerships.
However, he acknowledged that the system continued to record false positives of around 15% to 20%, which could not be entirely eliminated.

María Buhigas, Chief City Architect of Barcelona, said coastal cities such as Mumbai must reconsider traditional infrastructure-led approaches to protecting waterfronts against rising sea levels, intense rainfall and increasingly powerful waves.

articles.title: Nvidia's accounting is a focus of U.S. SEC investigation, sources say
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The SEC under U.S. President Donald Trump has pulled back ‌on enforcement, saying it will focus on bread-and-butter securities fraud
The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is probing Nvidia’s accounting practices, said two people briefed on the matter, adding to the legal woes facing the scandal-hit chip ​giant.

The Wall Street Journal on Tuesday reported that the SEC was probing Nvidia but said it could not ascertain the focus of the investigation. ‌The people, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential issues, said SEC ​enforcement staff are scrutinising potential accounting issues at the company.
A spokesperson for the SEC declined to comment. Spokespeople for ⁠Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Prices of Nvidia shares extended losses and were down about 13% on Friday, according to LSEG data, after Reuters reported details of the SEC probe. They had been down more than 6% before Reuters published its report.

Reuters could ‌not immediately determine when the SEC opened its inquiry or exactly what potential accounting issues the watchdog is examining. Investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing and many close without resulting in enforcement action.

Still, the accounting focus of the ‌probe, which Reuters is reporting for the first time, increases pressure on Nvidia, whose investors are still reeling from ‌revelations ⁠about ousted CEO Jensen Huang’s extramarital relationships, including with Alice Huang, who U.S. authorities suspect is a Chinese ⁠spy. China has denied she is a spy.

Alice Huang led Singapore-based Megaspeed, historically a large Nvidia chip customer, people familiar with the matter have said. U.S. authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since 2024 over possible violations of export controls related to alleged shipments of Nvidia AI chips to China, the U.S. Justice and Commerce ​departments said this week.
The crisis has sent shares ‌in Nvidia, a linchpin of the AI boom, tumbling more than a third and stoked calls in Washington for tougher action on tech threats posed by Beijing.

Megaspeed has said Alice Huang left the company in August 2025 and that it conducted “lawful business.” Reuters has not been able to reach Alice Huang. Jensen Huang admitted to an affair in a November ‌8 statement following the reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, without referring to her by name.

The SEC ​probe is the latest of Nvidia’s legal woes. The Justice Department has also been reviewing Nvidia’s $12.9-billion deal to buy open-source platform Hugging Face alongside a broader antitrust investigation into the company’s acquisitions and practices, Reuters ⁠reported last month.

Last year, Nvidia changed how it reports geographic revenue, using customer headquarters rather than billing addresses, which it said would better reflect the geographic profile of its revenue. The change resulted in Singapore being removed from ‌its geographical breakdown.
The Financial Times, citing company accounts, reported on Tuesday that Nvidia had made the change even as Singapore sales soared to almost half its global revenue.

The SEC under U.S. President Donald Trump has pulled back ‌on enforcement, saying it will focus on bread-and-butter securities fraud

The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is probing Nvidia’s accounting practices, said two people briefed on the matter, adding to the legal woes facing the scandal-hit chip ​giant.

The Wall Street Journal on Tuesday reported that the SEC was probing Nvidia but said it could not ascertain the focus of the investigation. ‌The people, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential issues, said SEC ​enforcement staff are scrutinising potential accounting issues at the company.

A spokesperson for the SEC declined to comment. Spokespeople for ⁠Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Prices of Nvidia shares extended losses and were down about 13% on Friday, according to LSEG data, after Reuters reported details of the SEC probe. They had been down more than 6% before Reuters published its report.

Reuters could ‌not immediately determine when the SEC opened its inquiry or exactly what potential accounting issues the watchdog is examining. Investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing and many close without resulting in enforcement action.

Still, the accounting focus of the ‌probe, which Reuters is reporting for the first time, increases pressure on Nvidia, whose investors are still reeling from ‌revelations ⁠about ousted CEO Jensen Huang’s extramarital relationships, including with Alice Huang, who U.S. authorities suspect is a Chinese ⁠spy. China has denied she is a spy.

Alice Huang led Singapore-based Megaspeed, historically a large Nvidia chip customer, people familiar with the matter have said. U.S. authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since 2024 over possible violations of export controls related to alleged shipments of Nvidia AI chips to China, the U.S. Justice and Commerce ​departments said this week.

The crisis has sent shares ‌in Nvidia, a linchpin of the AI boom, tumbling more than a third and stoked calls in Washington for tougher action on tech threats posed by Beijing.

Megaspeed has said Alice Huang left the company in August 2025 and that it conducted “lawful business.” Reuters has not been able to reach Alice Huang. Jensen Huang admitted to an affair in a November ‌8 statement following the reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, without referring to her by name.

The SEC ​probe is the latest of Nvidia’s legal woes. The Justice Department has also been reviewing Nvidia’s $12.9-billion deal to buy open-source platform Hugging Face alongside a broader antitrust investigation into the company’s acquisitions and practices, Reuters ⁠reported last month.

Last year, Nvidia changed how it reports geographic revenue, using customer headquarters rather than billing addresses, which it said would better reflect the geographic profile of its revenue. The change resulted in Singapore being removed from ‌its geographical breakdown.

The Financial Times, citing company accounts, reported on Tuesday that Nvidia had made the change even as Singapore sales soared to almost half its global revenue.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is probing Nvidia’s accounting practices, said two people briefed on the matter, adding to the legal woes facing the scandal-hit chip ​giant.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Financial Times, citing company accounts, reported on Tuesday that Nvidia had made the change even as Singapore sales soared to almost half its global revenue.

articles.title: Karnataka to make fresh bid for ST status for Kadugolla and Hattigolla communities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The State Cabinet, chaired by CM D.K. Shivakumar on November 19, decided to renew its recommendation to the Union Government after obtaining fresh evidence through a comprehensive ethnographic study

The Karnataka Government will make a fresh attempt to secure Scheduled Tribe (ST) status for the Kadugolla (Adavigolla) and Hattigolla communities after five rejections of its earlier proposals by the Centre.

The State Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on November 19, decided to renew its recommendation to the Union Government after obtaining fresh evidence through a comprehensive ethnographic study.

The study has been entrusted to the Centre for Multi-Disciplinary Development Research (CMDR), Dharwad. A team of anthropologists will document the community’s social structure, cultural practices, traditions and way of life. The Department of Scheduled Tribes Welfare has directed the institution to submit its report within three months.

The Director of the Scheduled Tribes Welfare Department and the Director of the Karnataka State Tribal Research Institute, Mysuru, will coordinate the exercise. The findings will be used to prepare a fresh proposal addressing the objections raised by the Centre.

Karnataka has been pursuing the demand for inclusion of the Kadugolla community in the ST list since 2015. The State sent proposals and additional communications to the Union Ministry of Tribal Affairs between March 2015 and April 2025.

However, the Office of the Registrar General of India (ORGI) declined to recommend the proposal on five occasions, in February 2017, February 2019, September 2022, March 2024 and June 2026. The principal objection was that the State had not provided sufficient new information or evidence to justify the inclusion, according to an official statement.

The Union Government issued revised guidelines for inclusion of communities in the ST list in September 2022. Under the prescribed procedure, a favourable recommendation from the ORGI is necessary for a proposal to move forward. The Union Ministry of Tribal Affairs formally rejected Karnataka’s proposal on July 22, 2026.

Union Minister of State for Railways and Jal Shakti V. Somanna wrote to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on October 7 and 30, pointing out shortcomings in the earlier submissions. He reportedly said the State had resubmitted information that had already been examined and advised it to constitute an expert committee to prepare a comprehensive report.
The latest Cabinet decision follows these communications and the State’s move to support its demand with fresh research.

articles.title: Karnataka Chief Minister to lead delegation to Japan for investment talks and urban-planning study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The visit will focus on two areas: attracting fresh investments from Japanese companies and understanding Japan’s approach to urban planning, transport, waste management, and infrastructure development

Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar will lead a high-level Karnataka government delegation to Japan from November 23 to 25 to explore investment opportunities and study the country’s urban development models for possible adoption in Bengaluru and other cities in the State.

The delegation will visit Nagoya on November 23, Osaka on November 24, and Tokyo on November 25. The visit will focus on two areas: attracting fresh investments from Japanese companies and understanding Japan’s approach to urban planning, transport, waste management, and infrastructure development.

Industries and Infrastructure Development Minister M.B. Patil will accompany the Chief Minister and lead the industrial engagements. He will also head the State’s investment promotion efforts in Japan and South Korea.

According to an official statement, the Chief Minister and the Commerce and Industries Department officials will hold meetings with senior representatives of leading Japanese companies to discuss their investment plans and showcase opportunities in Karnataka.
The discussions will cover sectors such as automobiles and electric vehicle components, speciality chemicals, advanced materials, pharmaceuticals, industrial automation and manufacturing.

The companies include Toyota and Panasonic Automotive Systems in the automobile and EV components sector, Mitsubishi Chemical Group, Takeda Pharmaceuticals, Yokogawa Electric and Sumitomo Corporation.

The State delegation will present Karnataka’s industrial policies and incentives, including its Aerospace and Defence policy, additional capital subsidy of up to 20% for investments in backward and priority taluks, the KIADB Digital Industrial Land Bank and the single-window clearance system.

The delegation will also meet the Executive Vice-President of the Japan External Trade Organisation (JETRO) to discuss ways to strengthen institutional support for Japanese companies looking to invest in Karnataka.
The companies will be invited to the Global Investors Meet 2027, organised by Invest Karnataka, which will be held at Bengaluru Palace from April 20 to 22.

The delegation, along with officials of the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA), will study Japan’s urban development practices, particularly in waste management, waste-to-energy, urban planning, public transport and transit planning, architecture and urban design.

Tokyo and Osaka have been selected for their experience in managing large urban populations and developing integrated infrastructure. Tokyo is known for its integrated transport network and redevelopment around railway stations, while Osaka offers examples of large-scale urban renewal and metropolitan planning.
As part of the visit, the delegation will visit Tokyo Midtown Roppongi along with representatives of Nikken Sekkei, a leading Japanese architecture and urban design firm, the statement said.

articles.title: Rajasthan panchayat polls: BJP's urban gains fail to translate into rural support
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The outcome is particularly significant as several BJP ministers faced electoral setbacks in their areas of influence

The BJP's strong performance in Rajasthan's urban local body elections failed to translate into a similar electoral advantage in rural areas, as panchayat polls exposed gaps in the ruling party's grassroots support
The outcome is particularly significant as several BJP ministers faced electoral setbacks in their areas of influence.

Family members of Urban Development and Housing Minister Jhabar Singh Kharra lost, while former BJP minister Rajendra Rathore’s son and daughter-in-law won. Overall, 17 State ministers and three Union ministers failed to secure the political ground they sought to defend.

The BJP suffered electoral defeats in Deputy Chief Minister Premchand Bairwa's Dudu Assembly constituency, Health Minister Gajendra Singh Khinvsar's Lohawat constituency and Agriculture Minister Kirodi Lal Meena's Sawai Madhopur constituency, indicating that the influence of prominent leaders did not necessarily translate into electoral support at the grassroots level.
The Congress, on the other hand, made significant gains in the rural polls, winning 794 of the 1,271 zila parishad seats and 3,758 of the 7,520 panchayat samiti seats..
The BJP secured 357 zila parishad seats and 2,213 panchayat samiti seats, while the Rashtriya Loktantrik Party (RLP) won 51 and 497 seats, respectively.
After the declaration of poll results, the Congress is in a position to elect more pradhans in panchayat samitis than the BJP and the RLP.
The election of zila pramukhs will take place on November 25, while panchayat samiti pradhans will be elected on November 27.
The rural verdict contrasts with the BJP's performance in the previous urban local body elections and underlines the distinct dynamics of urban and rural politics in Rajasthan.

While urban electoral contests may be shaped by broader political narratives and civic issues in towns and cities, panchayat elections are often influenced by local leadership, accessibility of elected representatives, community equations and everyday concerns of villagers.

The results also suggest that the BJP's position in government and its performance in urban bodies were not enough to insulate it from rural dissatisfaction. Issues such as roads, drinking water, electricity, encroachments and delays in routine public works are believed to have influenced voting in several areas.

Political leaders said dissatisfaction with local legislators and officials, factionalism and weak communication between grassroots workers and the party leadership may also have contributed to the ruling party's setbacks.

articles.title: Thousands of govt staff, teachers lay siege to Keralam Secretariat demanding service benefits, pay revision
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Protest organised by Action Council of State Employees and Teachers. Inaugurating the agitation, Opposition Leader Pinarayi Vijayan said the siege was a stern warning to State government against 'denying employees their legitimate rights’

Thousands of State government employees and teachers affiliated with Left-backed service organisations laid siege to the Secretariat here on Saturday, demanding immediate pay revision, withdrawal of the contributory pension scheme and restoration of various service benefits, among other demands. The protest, organised by the Action Council of State Employees and Teachers, saw participants assembling around the Secretariat premises.

Inaugurating the agitation, Opposition Leader Pinarayi Vijayan said the Secretariat siege was a stern warning to the State government against “denying employees their legitimate rights.” The United Democratic Front (UDF) government is an example of how an administration should not function,” he said, citing “a lack of mutual trust even within the Cabinet.”

Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan addresses a gathering of State employees and teachers during the official inauguration of their protest march outside the Secretariat on Saturday | Photo Credit: Nirmal Harindran

He also said several problems were bound to arise when a government failed to take the civil service into confidence. Stressing the need to repose trust in government officials, he alleged that the present administration viewed them as “adversaries.”

A satisfied civil service was essential for the State’s progress, he said, alleging that the UDF government had begun transferring officials indiscriminately soon after assuming office, disregarding established norms. While acknowledging the government’s authority to effect transfers, he said such powers should be exercised with discretion.

The agitation was organised to press for a slew of demands, including immediate pay revision and interim relief, withdrawal of the contributory pension scheme, disbursement of pending dearness allowance (DA) arrears, cancellation of arbitrary transfers and conduct of general transfers in accordance with established norms. The protesters also demanded rectification of deficiencies in the MEDISEP health insurance scheme and withdrawal of measures that undermine the service sector.

Meanwhile, Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala criticised the protest, pointing out the “irony of a former Chief Minister” inaugurating an agitation for pay revision despite failing to implement it during his 10-year tenure.

He also alleged that the previous government had withheld several benefits due to employees and questioned the need for such a massive agitation against a government that had been in office for less than six months.

articles.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon taking on Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Google said the new model was built for complex coding, analytical reasoning, and enterprise workflows
Google has launched a new AI model, Gemini 4 Neon, that it said was primed for complex software engineering, knowledge work, and science workflows.
According to the company, Neon ranked ahead of comparable models, including Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Sol, on several benchmarks.
Gemini 4 Neon is priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens with a million-token context window.
Google noted that the new model was designed to support long-running agentic workflows and ensure that tasks are completed, while balancing out costs.
Meanwhile users of the Gemini app could expect better writing and knowledge work, reliable research, and faster responses when faced with challenging tasks, per the company.

“Get more done while stretching usage limits further when handing off tedious to-dos, like analysing billing statements to spot why a utility charge spiked or cross-checking multiple receipts and documents to negotiate a refund,” suggested Google in a blog post.
The search giant affirmed that its new model maintained Gemini 4 Carbon-level safeguards against severe misuse and prompt injection, and also advanced model alignment.

“Neon is built for complex coding, analytical reasoning, and production-grade enterprise workflows. While Carbon tackles your hardest, long-horizon projects, and Hydrogen handles fast everyday execution, Neon balances depth and efficiency. Neon delivers frontier-level reasoning for complex, high-frequency workflows faster and more cost efficiently,” stated Koray Kavukcuoglu, SVP, Google DeepMind and Chief AI Architect at Google.

articles.title: U.S. court dispatches summonses to Doval, Goel in Pannun case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Indian Code of Civil Procedure permits summonses issued by foreign civil courts designated by notification of the Central Government of India to be transmitted to Indian courts and served as though issued by those courts

A U.S. court has dispatched summonses to National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and former Research and Analysis Wing Director Samant Goel in connection with a case involving Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun.
Pannun is wanted by Indian probe agencies on various terror charges.

The clerk of the Southern District Court of New York said that the summonses were sent through FedEx to the Patiala House Court, Tis Hazari Court, and the Dwarka District Court in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026).
On November 13, the Southern District Court of New York ordered that summonses be issued to Mr. Doval and Mr. Goel, citing the Hague Convention.

“The Court respectfully requests the assistance of receiving Indian courts in effecting service of process upon the defendants in this civil action pending before this court,” read an order by Judge Katherine Polk Failla.
Judge Failla cited the Hague Conventions and relevant sections of the Indian Code of Civil Procedure to state that foreign courts can serve summonses on Mr. Doval and Mr. Goel through Indian courts.

The Indian Code of Civil Procedure permits summonses issued by foreign civil courts designated by notification of the Central Government of India to be transmitted to Indian courts and served as though issued by those courts.

The order states that standard service through India's central authority under the Hague Convention was attempted but rejected. The Court then authorised alternative service under Article 19 of the Hague Convention and India's Code of Civil Procedure.
Pannun, legal counsel for the banned organisation Sikhs for Justice (SFJ), has filed the civil lawsuit seeking damages over an alleged attempt on his life.
He has accused Mr. Doval of orchestrating a plot involving India's foreign intelligence agency to assassinate him.
Last month, the U.S. court attempted to serve the summonses on Mr. Doval and Mr. Goel via a diplomatic note issued by the State Department to the Indian Embassy in Washington.
India has rejected Pannun’s lawsuit, calling it “fabricated and malicious”.

The Telangana government has issued guidelines for enrolment under the Indiramma Kutumba Jeevitha Bima Padhakam (IKJBP), which provides life insurance coverage of ₹5 lakh to one member of each eligible household, following the launch of the scheme by Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy in Siddipet on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

articles.title: Adani Defence fires four anti-tank missiles in Pokhran Test Range
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The missile is capable of engaging armour at up to 8 km, twice the approximately 4 km range of the land-based anti-tank missile

Adani Defence & Aerospace, the Adani Group's flagship defence and aerospace company, successfully demonstrated Bagheera AT1, a vehicle-mounted anti-tank guided missile (ATGM) system, at the Pokhran Field Firing Ranges in Rajasthan.

"The programme validated day and night engagements, a two-missile tandem firing along a single beam against a target representing an armoured vehicle, and an aerial-target engagement at an extended range. It was followed by a static display of the complete system," the company said in a statement.
The No Cost No Commitment (NCNC) demonstration at Pokhran on November 20 was witnessed by senior representatives of the Indian Army, Department of Military Affairs and Ministry of Defence (MoD).

"Bagheera AT1 is the outcome of 18 months of design and development, during which Adani Defence customised the missile system for Indian terrain, climate and operational requirements. The result is a complete combat system comprising the missile, automated launcher, day and night sights, mounted on an Adani Defence- designed 4x4 high-mobility armoured vehicle," it said.

The missile is capable of engaging armour at up to 8 km, twice the approximately 4 km range of the land-based anti-tank missile. It rides a laser beam rather than relying on a radio link, making it highly resistant to electronic jamming on a battlefield increasingly shaped by drones and electronic warfare.

The company said two missiles can be fired in quick succession along the same beam at a single target. "The first engages the tank's Active Protection System (APS), while the second is designed to penetrate its defences."

Four ready-to-fire missiles on the automated launcher and 8 reloads onboard, providing a total capacity of 12 missiles per vehicle. Also, integrated day television and thermal-imaging sights with automated target tracking. The crew engages from cover and relocates quickly to reduce exposure to enemy fire.
"The system can also engage aerial targets at extended range," the statement said.
India's requirement for modern anti-tank guided missiles remains substantial, with reported gaps in the ATGM inventory underscoring the need for continued modernisation.
The in-service backbone remains second-generation Milan-2T and Konkurs-M, with Spike missiles subsequently inducted to address immediate operational requirements.
India is also progressing with the acquisition of Javelin systems.

"Recent conflicts have underscored the importance of range and mobility in armoured engagements. Bagheera AT1 offers the Army an additional long-range, mobile ground capability alongside man-portable and helicopter-launched missiles," the firm said.

articles.title: From administrative reforms to AI policy to green economy, Keralam’s fifth Administrative Reforms Commission has a wide-ranging mandate
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The newly-constituted fifth ARC is required, among other things, to place recommendations for a State AI Policy and connected legal framework and examine “emerging challenges”

From administrative reforms to artificial intelligence (AI) policy to green economy, Keralam’s fifth Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC) has a more expansive mandate compared to the fourth ARC. The newly-constituted fifth ARC headed by former Minister and IUML leader M.K. Muneer is required, among other things, to place recommendations for a State AI Policy and connected legal framework and examine “emerging challenges” as wide-ranging as demographic ageing, migration, urbanisation, disaster and climate resilience and public health preparedness to green economy, Centre-State relations and fiscal federalism.

Published through a November 19 order of the Personnel and Administrative Reforms department, the terms of reference (ToR) for the panel appear to be a more expansive mandate compared to that of the fourth Commission headed by former Chief Minister V.S. Achuthanandan. The panel’s ToR require it to review the structure and processes of State administration against the backdrop of policy changes, institutional developments and technological advances that have taken place since the tenure of the previous Commission. Other ToR requirements include updating the Manual of Office Procedure and the Rules of Business of the government in line with “current policy, Acts and Rules.”
It will assess the implementation of earlier ARC recommendations, while suggesting reforms to make the State administration “adaptive, citizen-centred, efficient, accountable and future-ready.”

In the area of budgeting and planning, the panel should recommend “agile planning and budgeting mechanisms” that help the government adapt to unforeseen sectoral requirements. The panel will also look into the barriers hindering inter-departmental coordination and the interface between departments and local governments.
The Congress-led UDF government in Keralam had issued orders on October 1, 2026, constituting the fifth ARC chaired by Mr. Muneer.

The number of posts for the fifth ARC and that of the personal staff to the ARC chairman will be the same as that of the fourth ARC. The Personnel and Administrative Reforms department has issued orders for the creation of 12 posts for the new ARC including that of an Additional Secretary and Deputy Collector. In addition to these, there will be four daily-wage posts. The ARC chairman will have 12 personal staff whose appointments will be on a co-terminus basis.

articles.title: Karnataka government seeks action against Power TV over sting operations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The direction follows a complaint submitted by C.B. Suresh Babu, leader of the Karnataka Janata Dal (Secular) Legislature Party, to the Governor on November 3, seeking action against the private television channel for allegedly attempting to lure ministers and legislators with monetary inducements to record sting operations

The Karnataka government has directed the Director General and Inspector General of Police (DG & IGP) to examine allegations of blackmail, extortion and entrapment levelled against Power TV chief Rakesh Shetty and employees involved in the channel’s sting operations targeting elected representatives.

The direction follows a complaint submitted by C.B. Suresh Babu, leader of the Karnataka Janata Dal (Secular) Legislature Party, to the Governor on November 3, seeking action against the private television channel for allegedly attempting to lure ministers and legislators with monetary inducements to record sting operations.

In a communication dated November 20, the Home Department’s Under Secretary (Crimes), S. Ambika, forwarded the complaint and its enclosures to the Director General and Inspector General of Police, asking the police chief to examine the allegations in accordance with the law, take necessary action and submit a detailed action-taken report to the government.

According to Mr. Suresh Babu’s complaint, the channel allegedly devised a fictitious government scheme involving the installation of optical fibre cable (OFC) in March 2023 and approached nearly 33 legislators under the banner of its programme “Power Bete.” The complaint alleges that ministers and MLAs were offered money to facilitate the implementation of the purported scheme and were subsequently portrayed in a negative light through the sting operation.

The complaint also refers to a recent sting operation involving Hassan MLA Swaroop Prakash. It alleges that the channel’s team approached his office claiming that funds under the Scheduled Caste Sub-Plan (SCSP), Tribal Sub-Plan (TSP) and Minority Welfare Department schemes could be sanctioned for his constituency in return for a five per cent commission.

Mr. Suresh Babu has alleged that the channel’s team offered and handed over money to the MLA, recorded the interaction and subsequently telecast the footage. He has claimed that the MLA did not demand money or negotiate any financial transaction and was instead induced into the situation by the sting operation team.

The representation argues that the alleged use of fictitious schemes and monetary inducements amounted to entrapment rather than a genuine exercise to expose corruption. It also raises concerns over violation of the privacy and dignity of elected representatives and misuse of the freedom of the press.

The complaint names several serving and former ministers and legislators who were allegedly targeted in the 2023 sting operation and refers to other opposition legislators, including Swaroop Prakash, in connection with the 2026 operation.

Meanwhile, a senior police official said the government’s communication had been forwarded to the Chief Commissioner of Police (CCP) for further action. The Cyber Crime wing of the Central Crime Branch (CCB) was already investigating the case, the official said.

articles.title: European Union proposes tax on Big Tech to boost budget
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: European Council president Antonio Costa unveiled a new spending proposal that slashes by 204 billion euros a plan initially put forward by the European Commission

The European Union (EU) put forward plans to tax the world's biggest digital companies to fund its next budget on Saturday (November 21, 2026), as it seeks to bridge divisions among member states over the bloc's long-term funding.

European Council president Antonio Costa unveiled a new spending proposal that slashes by 204 billion euros ($224 billion) a plan initially put forward by the European Commission, which some countries had slammed as too onerous.
"I believe this proposal can bring us closer to a final agreement," Mr. Costa told a press conference in Brussels.

EU countries have been squabbling over the size of the next budget, with Germany leading calls for major cuts after the Commission last year proposed a two-trillion-euro budget for the 2028-2034 period.
Berlin criticised a revised proposal published last month that suggested slashing the bloc's future seven-year budget by 140 billion euros.
Mr. Costa, who represents the EU's 27 states, is seeking to reach a deal by the end of the year balancing contributions from member states with new sources of revenue for the bloc.

Among these could be a tax on digital firms that the draft Mr. Costa presented on Saturday says will concern companies with an annual turnover for digital activities of at least 50 million euros in the EU as well as a global turnover of more than 750 million euros.

They would be subjected to "an annual contribution corresponding to 3% of the annual net turnover from online advertising, digital intermediation services and user-generated data", according to documents shared by the council.

The plan is likely to provoke U.S. President Donald Trump's ire since his administration has reacted angrily to EU fines and moves against Big Tech under its content and competition rules in recent years. The draft also includes plans for a levy on electronic waste and higher tobacco taxes.
The document will be at the centre of hours of fraught talks when EU leaders meet in Brussels next week.

Mr. Costa is pushing for a deal in December, amid EU fears that a delay would push talks into a fraught election year in 2027 with worries about what potential eurosceptic victories in France and elsewhere would mean for future deal-making.
Once EU states find an agreement, they will have to negotiate with Parliament — a task that also promises to be difficult.

articles.title: Iran says allies China, Russia oppose change in nuclear doctrine
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Iran has barred the International Atomic Energy Agency from inspecting its nuclear sites, citing security concerns and blaming the agency for failing to condemn U.S. and Israeli attacks on its nuclear facilities
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said China and Russia oppose a change in Tehran’s nuclear doctrine, amid domestic calls for a shift, state media reported.
In an interview published on Saturday (November 21, 2026), Mr. Araghchi told the state-run Iran Daily newspaper that the issue was “broad, serious” and had its own “supporters and opponents”.
“Russia and China are also opposed” to a change in Iran’s doctrine, he added. Both countries have strategic cooperation agreements with Iran.
“What matters is that, up to this point, our doctrine has not changed, and our official positions remain the same as before,” Mr. Araghchi said.

Debate over changing Iran’s nuclear doctrine has resurfaced in the country’s political circles, particularly among hardliners, following wars with Israel and the United States that saw Iranian nuclear facilities come under heavy attack.
Some advocates of a shift argue that it would pave the way for Tehran to develop a nuclear weapon as a deterrent.

Iran has barred the International Atomic Energy Agency from inspecting its nuclear sites, citing security concerns and blaming the agency for failing to condemn U.S. and Israeli attacks on its nuclear facilities.
Last week, the UN nuclear watchdog urged Iran to take “incremental steps” to allow inspectors to return to key facilities, saying such access was “critical”.

Iranian officials continue to cite a fatwa, or religious decree, issued by former supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei that prohibited the development of weapons of mass destruction, including nuclear weapons.

“There are those who believe the country’s nuclear doctrine should be maintained in its current form, and others who speak of the need to change it. Both sides have their own arguments and rationale,” Mr. Araghchi said.
Mr. Khamenei was killed in a U.S.-Israeli strike on his compound in central Tehran on February 28, triggering a regional war as Iran responded with missile and drone attacks across the West Asia.
His successor and son, Mojtaba Khamenei, who has remained out of public view since his appointment in March, has not issued a decree that would overturn his father’s ruling.

articles.title: Iran-U.S. negotiations stalled over uranium enrichment dispute, mediators warn of renewed conflict, says reports
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The diplomatic deadlock comes amid continuing tensions between Washington and Tehran, with both countries yet to reach an understanding on the future of Iran's nuclear programme

Negotiations between the United States and Iran have stalled over disagreements concerning Tehran's enriched uranium stockpile , with mediators warning that they cannot guarantee a return to military escalation in West Asia.

Washington is insisting on a clear roadmap and written guarantees from Iran that it will eliminate its enriched uranium stockpile and refrain from resuming uranium enrichment in the future, Al Arabiya English reported, citing a senior source. However, both sides have maintained firm positions on the issue despite several proposals put forward by mediators to bridge their differences, the report said.

The diplomatic deadlock comes amid continuing tensions between Washington and Tehran, with both countries yet to reach an understanding on the future of Iran's nuclear programme. Earlier, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran would not accept an agreement with Washington merely to end the current diplomatic impasse, insisting that any settlement must protect Iran's national interests and provide assurances against another military confrontation.

In an interview with an Iranian state-run newspaper, as reported by Al Jazeera , Mr. Araghchi said Iran was seeking a "good, honourable and lasting agreement" rather than remaining in a situation of "neither war nor peace". Questioning the durability of any potential understanding with Washington, he said, "What is the point of reaching an agreement today if it is violated two months later and war resumes?" Mr. Araghchi recalled that fighting had resumed just 15 days after the June ceasefire agreement, arguing that Tehran would not accept an arrangement simply to escape the current situation.
Iran strikes U.S. air base in Kuwait, targets Bahrain amid wider Gulf attacks
A step back: On Trump’s no-war, no-deal approach against Iran

On the nuclear issue, the Iranian Foreign Minister said Tehran was open to negotiations over its stockpile of uranium enriched to 60% but ruled out transferring the material outside the country. He maintained that a fair formula could be reached on uranium enrichment, provided it formed part of a broader agreement addressing Iran's national interests and security concerns.

Mr. Araghchi also confirmed that Tehran and Washington continued exchanging messages and proposals through mediators, including Qatar and Pakistan. "We are people of diplomacy, and we still have hope in diplomacy," he said.

Meanwhile, he maintained that Iran remained willing to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if Washington fulfilled its conditions, underlining Tehran's position that any diplomatic settlement must address its nuclear programme, sanctions and security concerns.

articles.title: Bangladesh Minister vows action against those behind arson, blames Awami League-linked groups, says reports
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Humaiun Kobir said law enforcement agencies were working to bring those responsible to justice and alleged that the Awami League’s leadership, including those based abroad, was encouraging the attacks

Bangladesh will take firm legal action against those behind recent arson and petrol bomb attacks, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir has said, blaming groups linked to the banned Awami League for the violence amid escalating political unrest in the country, according to local media reports.

Mr. Kobir, on Friday (November 20, 2026), said law enforcement agencies were working to bring those responsible to justice and alleged that the Awami League's leadership, including those based abroad, was encouraging the attacks.

"We will go after these terrorists, and the long arm of justice will reach them," he said, responding to questions from reporters on the sidelines of a media briefing, according to the state-run BSS news agency.
Mr. Kobir alleged that the Awami League leadership was encouraging the attacks from abroad and that others based overseas were also involved in efforts to instigate violence.
The Minister’s remarks come amid a spate of political violence and arson attacks across Bangladesh.

At least four people were killed in separate incidents earlier this week, including three leaders of the ruling BNP and its affiliated organisations and a bus helper who was burnt alive after unidentified assailants set fire to parked buses, the Dhaka Tribune reported.

In separate remarks at the Foreign Ministry, Mr. Kobir described the Awami League, whose political activities remain banned, as a "terrorist organisation" and warned of strong action against those involved in petrol bomb attacks, arson and other violence, The Daily Star reported.

articles.title: Study highlights need for trauma-informed, community-based mental health support for refugees in India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The study calls for mental health support rooted in refugee communities, with trained local workers and refugee leaders playing a central role in shaping care that responds to their lived realities, including legal uncertainty, social exclusion and difficult living conditions

Mental health concerns among refugee communities are linked not only to past trauma, violence and forced displacement but also to legal uncertainty, limited work opportunities, poor living conditions and social isolation in host countries, finds a study of Sri Lankan Tamil and Rohingya communities in India, published in the International Journal of Migration, Health and Social Care.

Titled ‘Building mental health capacity in protracted refugee situations: Empirical pointers from Sri Lankan Tamil and Rohingya populations in India’, the study looks at common mental health concerns and barriers to accessing care. It calls for training community members and health workers to recognise psychological distress, provide basic support and facilitate access to professional mental health services.

articles.title: South Korea confirms first case of cholera in 10 years
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: It is the country's first case of cholera since 2016, when authorities identified three cases suspected to be caused by contaminated seafood. At least 162 people got sick in a larger outbreak in 2001
South Korea on Friday reported its first case of cholera in 10 years, with health authorities urging people to take precautionary measures, use only safe water and wash their food properly.

The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency said health workers confirmed cholera from test samples of a person who had visited a hospital emergency room in the southeastern port city of Changwon earlier this month, showing symptoms of vomiting and diarrhea.

The agency said the unidentified person, who recovered and was discharged on Tuesday, had not travelled overseas in the past two months. It said health workers were trying to trace the source of infection and the people the person had been in contact with.

It was the country's first case of cholera since 2016, when authorities identified three cases suspected to be caused by contaminated seafood. At least 162 people got sick in a larger outbreak in 2001.

The agency issued guidance urging people to stick to safe water and cooked food and to wash and peel fruits and vegetables. It also urged medical facilities to promptly test and report suspected cases.

articles.title: Strain-specific Ebola jab trials to start in DR Congo next week: WHO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: A total of 5,568 deaths out of 11,376 cases have been confirmed in the vast central African country's worst-ever Ebola outbreak, according to the WHO

Two potential vaccines against the deadly Ebola strain gripping the Democratic Republic of Congo are set to enter trials in the outbreak's epicentre next week, the World Health Organisation announced earlier this week.
There are currently no vaccines or treatments for the less common Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind the explosive outbreak declared in May, triggering an international public health emergency.
A total of 5,568 deaths out of 11,376 cases have been confirmed in the vast central African country's worst-ever Ebola outbreak, according to the WHO.

"We expect two candidate vaccines developed specifically for Bundibugyo virus to begin testing as early as next week," WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus told a press conference at the UN health agency's headquarters in Geneva.

The so-called Tumaini trial in the DRC is a single framework that can test the safety, efficacy and ability to trigger an immune response of multiple vaccines. The trial uses ring vaccination: immunising contacts deemed to be at high risk of infection.

Ervebo, a vaccine already approved for use against the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, kicked off the Tumaini trial on October 23, at the full-scale Phase 3 level, to determine if it also offers any protection against Bundibugyo.
The trial will now also incorporate the two Bundibugyo-specific candidate vaccines, which have both gone through earlier-stage, smaller-scale Phase 1 clinical trials.

One is a ChAdOx1 adenoviral vector jab developed by the University of Oxford; the other, mRNA-1469, was developed by the US-based Moderna group using the mRNA technology made famous during the Covid-19 pandemic.

Meg Doherty, head of the WHO's science for health department, said Phase 2 clinical trials with the candidate vaccines are scheduled to begin on November 26 or 27 in Bunia, the capital of the DRC's northeastern Ituri province at the epicentre of the outbreak.
If the safety and immune response data from the Phase 2 trial pass the next stage of review, the candidate jabs can move forward to a full-scale Phase 3 trial.

Doherty said that more than 140 people were enrolled in the Tumaini trial, with thousands of contacts ultimately expected to sign up. The trial will also eventually expand beyond the current single site in Bunia.
Ebola, which spreads through contact with bodily fluids and causes a haemorrhagic fever, has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the past 50 years.
