articles.title: TDP secures ZP chairperson, vice-chairperson posts in six Rayalaseema districts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Paritala Sriram, son of slain TDP leader Paritala Ravi, elected to the top post in Sri Sathya Sai district, where the vice-chairperson post goes to alliance partner JSP

Elections to the Zilla Parishad chairperson and vice-chairperson posts in the Rayalaseema districts of Chittoor, Annamayya, Sri Sathya Sai, Anantapur, Kurnool and Nandyal were conducted peacefully on Friday, with the TDP-led NDA securing the key posts.
With the NDA completely dominating the ZP elections, the YSRCP’s activity remained subdued.
The elections followed the completion of the ZPTC election process and witnessed political activity among the alliance parties over distribution of the top positions.
The TDP retained the chairperson posts in a majority of the districts, while Jana Sena Party was accommodated in the leadership arrangement in the Sri Sathya Sai district.

In Chittoor, TDP’s Madalam Sailaja was elected ZP chairperson and S. Manjupriya Venkatesh vice-chairperson. The chairperson post attracted interest among several aspirants, with the party leadership holding discussions before finalising the candidate.

In Annamayya district, Sugavasi Prasad Babu of the TDP was elected chairperson and Talari Saranya vice-chairperson. The selection followed discussions within the alliance on the composition of the ZP leadership.

In Sri Sathya Sai district, TDP sprang a surprise with Paritala Sriram, son of slain TDP leader Paritala Ravi and sitting Raptadu MLA Paritala Sunitha, elected ZP chairperson, while the vice-chairperson post went to the Jana Sena Party. The seat-sharing understanding between the alliance partners looked tough initially, but was sorted out after intense deliberations.
In Anantapur, TDP’s Ganje Nagaraju was elected chairperson and Vennapusa Lalitha vice-chairperson. The TDP had the numbers among the elected ZPTC members to secure the posts.

In Kurnool, Chudi Uligayya of the TDP was elected ZP chairperson and Dr. Shaik Sadhika vice-chairperson. The election was conducted peacefully, and the newly elected representatives took charge following the formal proceedings.
In Nandyal, Shaik Burhanuddin was elected the first ZP chairperson of the district, while Kotamreddy Srikanth Reddy became vice-chairperson.

articles.title: Centre to examine demand to exclude Piravanthur, Punnala from ESA draft
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Union Minister Bhupender Yadav has said that the ministry has officially recorded the concerns and suggestions for consideration and will review them thoroughly before issuing the final notification

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav has assured that the ministry will examine the demand to exclude Piravanthur and Punnala villages in Kollam district from the draft notification of the Western Ghats Ecologically Sensitive Area (ESA). In a formal reply to a letter submitted by Kodikunnil Suresh MP, the Union Minister said that the ministry has officially recorded the concerns and suggestions for consideration and will review them thoroughly before issuing the final notification.

The intervention was made to bring the apprehensions of local residents regarding the inclusion of Piravanthur and Punnala in the ESA to the Centre’s attention. The government was urged to ensure that steps taken in the name of environmental conservation do not adversely affect the lives and livelihoods of the people, emphasising that a final decision must only be reached after taking ground realities and public concerns into account.

articles.title: Russia says role for EU's Kallas in Ukraine talks with Moscow would lead to their collapse
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Zakharova told a press briefing in Moscow that Kallas was totally unsuitable to take part in such talks and listed ‌a series of statements from Kallas which she ​said showed the EU official was anti-Russian

Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said on ​Friday (November 20, 2026) that the participation of Kaja Kallas, the European Union's foreign ‌policy chief, in any potential future negotiations on ​Ukraine with Moscow would lead to the collapse ⁠of talks.

Ms. Kallas said earlier this month that Russia had no say over who represented the bloc in the Ukraine-Russia peace ‌talks, adding she knew Moscow did not want her there but that she spoke on ‌behalf of all 27 member states rather than ‌in ⁠a personal capacity.

Ms. Kallas has said Russia needs to ⁠agree to a ceasefire in Ukraine and make concessions before any serious peace talks can begin, and has been sceptical about Russia's ​desire to discuss Europe's own ‌security architecture as part of negotiations.

Ms. Zakharova told a press briefing in Moscow that Ms. Kallas was totally unsuitable to take part in such talks and listed ‌a series of statements from Ms. Kallas which she ​said showed the EU official was anti-Russian.

"If anyone in Brussels is interested in such a ⁠negotiator with Russia, it merely demonstrates to us clearly what results they hope to achieve in dialogue with us — ‌the derailment of any peace initiatives. That, it seems to me, is something she (Kallas) will carry out with flying colours," said Ms. Zakharova.

Europe has so far not been involved in U.S.-mediated peace talks between Russia and Ukraine, but has agreed it will be represented ‌by five major military powers — non-member Britain plus France, Germany, Italy ​and Poland — and EU institutions, if and when it is included. President Vladimir Putin said ⁠on Thursday (November 19, 2026) that Russia had proposed that European envoys come ⁠to Russia to clarify their position on peace negotiations before the format of further talks is decided. ‌Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said on Friday (November 20, 2026) that a potential visit to Moscow by representatives from ​Britain, Germany and France was being worked on.

articles.title: U.K., EU to announce youth mobility deal, as they discuss closer ties
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The two sides are expected to announce a scheme for 100,000 18-32 year olds to live and work across each other’s borders

U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham is expected to agree new terms for Britain’s relationship with the EU as he meets with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen in Brussels on November 20 at a Summit meeting. Mr Burnham has said in recent weeks that Brexit had caused “more harm than good”.

The two sides are expected to announce a scheme for 100,000 18-32 year olds to live and work across each other’s borders. In addition, they are working on closer ties in food and drink and linking the carbon trading schemes of the U.K. and the EU, as per reports.
“There’s the possibility of lower food prices, I can’t turn my back on that,” Mr Burnham said.
The summit is expected to announce the start of a dialogue on migration — including returns of irregular migrants to third countries.

The deal is a significant step to closer ties but is not expected to be the post-Brexit “reset” with Brussels that the Labour Party has sought . Mr Burnham, who is taking forward some of the discussions held with Brussels by his predecessor Keir Starmer, has committed to keeping to the red lines outlined in the Labour 2024 manifesto for the duration of this parliament (2029).

These red lines include not joining the bloc, nor its customs union and single market, and not allowing the “free movement” of people across UK-EU borders. However, Mr Burnham has said the U.K. would have to decide on its long-term options for its ties with the EU — including rejoining the EU The nature of the future relationship between the U.K. and EU is likely to be a campaign issue when Britain approaches its next general election.
“Business across the country have been clear, our current deal with the EU is not good enough,” said UK minister for EU relations, Hamish Falconer.

Mr Burnham had earlier said he would present legislation to the U.K. Parliament next week on this week’s agreements with Brussels. The U.K. will need harmonize some of its laws with the EU’s (i.e., follow them) to operationalize any deal on agriculture for instance.

articles.title: FDA sets up council for post-market review of vaccines, gene therapies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The FDA said the council is intended to improve accountability and transparency as biologic products grow increasingly complex, particularly in cell and gene therapy, a sector that has seen rapid regulatory expansion in recent years

The US Food and Drug Administration said on Thursday it had established a new internal safety body within its biologics center, formalizing independent oversight of approved products such as vaccines, gene therapies and blood products once they reach the market.

The CBER Safety Council will report directly to the director of the FDA’s Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, structurally separating post-market safety reviews from the offices responsible for approving those products, the agency said.

The council supersedes CBER’s existing Safety Working Group, bringing together senior scientific and regulatory officials to review safety signals, conduct benefit-risk assessments and recommend regulatory actions as warranted.

The new structure formalizes an independent post-market review process at a time when regulators face mounting pressure to closely monitor newer biologic products, including gene and cell therapies, after approval, when they are used across far broader patient populations.
Its mandate will cover emerging safety concerns, potential labeling changes, risk-management measures and safety-related post-market studies, as well as advising on potential market withdrawals.

The FDA said the council is intended to improve accountability and transparency as biologic products grow increasingly complex, particularly in cell and gene therapy, a sector that has seen rapid regulatory expansion in recent years.

The council will coordinate with external bodies including the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the National Institutes of Health, drawing on surveillance systems such as the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) and the FDA Sentinel program.
The council takes effect on November 19; the agency said additional details on its structure and membership will be released later.

articles.title: Watch | How has ‘Project Cheetah’ progressed in India?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: A video explainer on 'Project Cheetah', the first intercontinental transfer of wild cats into the country.

In September 2022, Prime Minister Narendra Modi released a coalition of cheetahs into the Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh. Eight cheetahs, five of which are female, were flown from Windhoek, Namibia, to Gwalior.

It was the first intercontinental transfer of wild cats into India since independence. The proposal for the project, known as ‘Project Cheetah’, was prepared in 2008-09 under the then PM Manmohan Singh.

The cheetahs were flown into India following several weeks of medical supervision in Namibia. They will be released into the wild gradually so that they have enough time to adapt to Indian conditions.

It also ensures reduced risk of contracting and spreading infection and hone the skills to hunt Indian prey. The eight cheetahs were housed in six enclosures, referred to as ‘bomas’ and were initially provided with buffalo meat.

All are expected to be moved inside larger enclosures in weeks. The cheetahs are radio-collared and their movements will be tracked. Each animal also has a dedicated tracking team. A team of wildlife scientists, biologists and zoologists are monitoring the initiative.

articles.title: Unions urge Railway Board to recognise Chief Loco Inspectors as running staff
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The long-pending demand to recognise Chief Loco Inspectors (CLIs) as part of the Loco Running cadre has resurfaced, with the South Central Railway Mazdoor Union and the National Federation of Railwaymen urging the Railway Board to take an early, reasoned decision.

Union general secretary M. Raghavaiah sought a clear clarification from the Board that CLIs are Loco Running Supervisors and should not be categorised as “non-running” or “stationary” staff. Such a classification, he said, had affected their morale and was contrary to existing railway rules and the duties they perform.

The union said running and maintenance supervisors once shared a common promotion channel, while some medically de-categorised running staff were accommodated in stationary posts. However, Railway Board instructions issued in November 1992 separated the two streams, stipulating that loco running supervisors would thereafter be drawn exclusively from the Loco Pilot cadre.

It argued that references to “stationary posts” in certain rules apply only to alternative appointments for medically de-categorised running staff and cannot be extended to serving CLIs who are promoted from the running cadre.

Mr. Raghavaiah said CLIs continue to perform supervisory duties linked to train operations, including training and monitoring running staff on locomotive footplates. The 30% pay element granted to them compensates for the reduction in running allowance earnings after promotion and reflects their continued association with running duties, the union said.

The union has urged the Railway Board to direct all zonal railways, production units and directorates to recognise CLIs as Loco Running Supervisors. “Around 400 CLIs across SCR (South Central Railway) and SCoR (South Coast Railway) deserve revision with retrospective effect, which they have been denied due to administrative inaction,” media coordinator V. Sripatisharma stated in a press release.

articles.title: Bengaluru Police Commissionerate restructuring leaves some divisions overburdened and others underutilised
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The newly created Peenya division has been the biggest casualty. Under the supervision of a single DCP, the division, which falls under the West Commissionerate, has only four police stations

The restructuring of the Bengaluru City Police Commissionerate into five parts has not only created confusion over the reporting structure, but has also resulted in an uneven distribution of police stations across divisions, with no clear rationale behind how stations were grouped.

The newly created Peenya division has been the biggest casualty. Under the supervision of a single Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP), the division, which falls under the West Commissionerate, has only four police stations: Peenya, Byadarahalli, Rajagopalnagar and Madanayakanahalli. Whitefield and East divisions had faced a similar situation, with five and six police stations, respectively.

Four police stations are usually handled by a single Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP). Ironically, the ACP of the Vijayanagar subdivision, which also falls under the West Commissionerate, oversees five police stations, one more than the DCP of Peenya.

Further, there had been a proposal to bring the Nelamangala police station within city limits. Its jurisdiction lies immediately beyond that of the Madanayakanahalli police station, and it could have been brought under city limits and placed within the Peenya division, but this was not done.

Moreover, the West Commissionerate has two other divisions, West and Kengeri, which have 13 and 11 police stations, respectively. A senior police officer said the Peenya division could have shared the burden of the other two divisions, which would have ensured that all three divisions had eight to nine police stations each. He described the exercise as “conceived without any ground-level understanding and background work”.
“The uneven division is a result of a hurried restructuring exercise. The exercise is not data-backed, and there have not been enough discussions,” he said.

Earlier this year, there was a proposal to add at least 15 more law-and-order police stations from the adjoining Bengaluru Rural and Bengaluru South district police units to the Bengaluru City Commissionerate.
The rationale was that these areas had largely urbanised, yet continued to be governed by rural police units. Seven of those police stations have now been added.

The police stations left out are Nelamangala, Doddaballapur, Devanahalli, Vijayapura, Vishwanathapura, Hoskote, Bidadi, Tavarekere and Kaggalipura. A senior police officer familiar with the developments said the stations left out were still considered semi-urban.
However, most of these areas have witnessed rapid commercialisation and the development of new layouts. In addition, several of them fall within the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) area.

Further, KWIN City is coming up in the Doddaballapur belt, which is likely to see further residential development. In Bidadi, a mega AI city project, known as the Greater Bidadi Integrated Township, is also coming up. However, the police stations covering these areas have not been included.

Before the erstwhile Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) was restructured into five corporations, the government had constituted the Brand Bengaluru Committee, which carried out the exercise, backed by data and stakeholder consultations, and submitted a report.

articles.title: ₹5,000 will reach eligible farmers by December 1: Parameshwara
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The entire sum of ₹5,000 drought relief announced for eligible farmers will be transferred in two instalments to their bank accounts by December 1, Deputy Chief Minister and Revenue Minister G. Parameshwara said.

Speaking to the media after reviewing the progress of the Revenue Department with Deputy Commissioners and other officials, he outlined the measures being taken by the State Government to address drought.

Mr. Parameshwara said all farmers included in the green list would receive both instalments of the relief by December 1. He said confusion had arisen because some officials had misunderstood the directions, but the issue had now been fully clarified.

State BJP president B.Y. Vijayendra had said that the Opposition would not allow the House proceedings if the farmers are not paid compensation before December 2, before the Legislature session begins in Belagavi.

Mr. Parameshwara stressed that there had been no response from the Centre on the ₹22,400.58 crore drought relief plea. “We have sought ₹22,400.58 crore from the Union government towards drought relief, but there has been no response so far. We have written seeking appointments with the Union Agriculture Minister, Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Prime Minister Narendra Modi, but have not received a reply. This does not reflect well on the Union government,” he said.

articles.title: BRS asks CM to check records as to which party allowed taking away Krishna water to non-basin areas
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Harish Rao says it was BRS that secured tribunal adjudication on Krishna water sharing afresh between Telugu States

Former Minister and Deputy Floor Leader of the BRS Legislature Party T. Harish Rao has stated that he is ready to prove with documentary evidence how the Congress government in the State let over 1,000 tmc ft of Godavari water flow down to Andhra Pradesh without meeting the needs of Telangana.

“We have already explained with evidence how over 1,000 tmc ft water was let go to A.P. Besides, A.P. is illegally constructing a tunnel from the right bank of Nagarjunasagar Project to tap more Krishna water. However, Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy hid that fact and it came to light because of BRS, KTR and a section of the print media,” Mr. Harish Rao said addressing a press conference here on Friday.

Every time the BRS corners Mr. Revanth Reddy and Irrigation Minister N. Uttam Kumar Reddy on their inaction on AP’s water theft, they bring out a back-dated letter. “When we raised the issue of Polavaram-Banakacherla Link Project, the government brought out a back-dated letter and washed off its hands,” the BRS leader said adding that the same thing had happened in case of the AP’s tunnel from Nagarjunasagar.

He recollected how under the Congress rule, the water discharge capacity of the Pothireddypadu Head Regulator was enhanced to about four times of its original capacity to take more water with gravity to the areas outside the basin in A.P. from Srisailam.

Let the Chief Minister check the records to learn facts about the Pothireddypadu issue, for which he blamed BRS (TRS) at Thursday’s Siddipet public meeting. He explained: “We resigned our ministerial posts in the YSR Cabinet on July 4, 2005 and the Pothireddypadu GO was issued on September, 2005 - i.e. 3 months after we walked out of the government.”

The TRS had moved an adjournment motion in the Assembly and stalled the proceedings for 40 days, after the GO was issued and only one Congress leader P. Janardhan Reddy stood with them, Mr. Harish Rao recollected.

He blamed that Congress for the real injustice to Telangana on Krishna waters as it was the same party that had fixed the ratio at 299 (Telangana):512 (AP) and the same ration was mentioned in the combined A.P. Government report to the Justice Srikrishna Commission in October 2013 and the same was placed before the Assembly for passing the AP Reorganisation Bill.
On the Siddipet public meeting he said, the Congress workers were moved from 26 constituencies and yet the government called it an official meeting on development/welfare works.

articles.title: Coal auction rounds attract 85 bids; 20 first-time players enter sector
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The 16th round of commercial mine auctions put forth 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.
The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions has attracted 83 bids for 17 coal blocks with 20 first-time bidders seeking to enter commercial coal mining, signalling fresh interest in the sector.
The Union Coal Ministry said on Friday that 17 blocks offered in the latest round received 83 bids. In addition, the second attempt to auction one coal block from the 15th round attracted two bids.
Taking the 26 blocks covered by the auction process into account, the number of bids has quadrupled compared with the previous round, the ministry said.
The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions was launched on September 17, offering 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.

“Competition in the current round has been intense, with 16 of the 26 blocks attracting multiple bids. The round has also brought 20 first-time bidders into the commercial coal mining regime, a clear sign that the sector continues to draw new capital and new players,” the ministry said in a statement.

Since the introduction of the commercial coal mining auction regime in June 2020, the government has auctioned 145 coal mines across 15 rounds. These mines are estimated to generate annual revenues of around ₹47,500 crore, according to government estimates.

articles.title: CEA flags need to align capital markets with India’s development priorities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Equity market capitalisation stood at around 130% of GDP, while the corporate bond market accounted for only about 16%.

Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran has called for a greater role for Indian capital markets in channelising household savings into productive investments, stressing the importance of patient capital in meeting the country’s long-term development needs.

Speaking at the CII Financial Summit in Mumbai, Mr. Nageswaran said sectors such as infrastructure, manufacturing, agriculture and mineral exploration required long-term financing, given their extended investment horizons.
Highlighting the imbalance in India’s financial markets, he pointed out that equity market capitalisation stood at around 130% of GDP, while the corporate bond market accounted for only about 16%.

While acknowledging that technology had improved market access, settlement systems and transaction security, he said these advances had not necessarily translated into better outcomes for investors or the real economy.

“A safer machine is not the same as a better outcome,” he said, emphasising that technological innovation should ultimately strengthen the capital market’s core function of converting savings into productive investments.
Cautioning against a consumption-led economic model, Mr. Nageswaran said, “An economy that is consumption-oriented may not be the most suited one for India’s development context.”

Echoing the need to promote long-term savings, Gaurav Mathur, founder and managing director of SafeGold, called for tax incentives to encourage investors to hold financial assets for longer periods. He stressed that savings policies should reflect individuals’ financial circumstances and different stages of life.

“It’s a matter of constructive partnership between regulators and financial intermediaries, where you incentivise long-term saving behaviour at the appropriate stages in life,” Mr. Mathur said, adding that incentives should particularly target wealthier individuals with greater capacity to save.

Meanwhile, Nilesh Shah, managing director of Kotak Mahindra Asset Management Company and part-time member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, underscored the need to strengthen financial literacy and encourage voluntary pension savings. He said these measures were increasingly important amid uncertainties over employment and income in a technology-driven economy.

articles.title: How AI could reshape global growth and productivity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: A key expected impact of AI is an unprecedented rise in labour productivity, as its success as a technological revolution is premised on such an increase; what remains to be seen is how pervasive its impact will be across different sectors of the economy

Many have likened the artificial intelligence (AI) phenomenon to the inventions of the steam engine or internal combustion engine in the 18th and 19th centuries, respectively. Only time can tell whether AI is epochal of that kind. In this two-part piece, we discuss the possible impact it may have on the global economy as a whole.

A key impact of AI is considered to be an unprecedented rise in labour productivity. In fact, if there is one purpose AI is supposed to serve, it is enhancing labour productivity multifold. Since labour productivity is a key variable in this puzzle, consider what it constitutes of (Box 1) . It is a ratio of output and workers employed. Now this ratio can rise in three different ways — a rise in output for a given number of workers employed (rise in the numerator); a loss of jobs which leads to a fall in the denominator; more jobs are created, but the output rises faster than the jobs (while both the numerator and the denominator are rising, the numerator rises faster than the denominator).

There is usually a distinction drawn between a case where there is a net loss of jobs versus one where jobs grow, but the output grows even faster. The latter is preferred over the former. Even though AI may displace white-collar workers, it may generate more jobs for the blue-collar workers, so in the net there may not be a job loss with AI adoption across the economy. However, for the argument we make below, it does not matter which of the three sources leads to a rise in productivity. Why should the rise in labour productivity matter? There are two contrasting takes on this question in the economics discipline.

One which argues that productivity growth increases the growth of output in the economy. The idea is simple. Growth of output is a function of its two inputs — labour and capital. Since capital enhances the productivity of labour, the rate at which output can grow is the sum of the growth of the labour force and its productivity. So, if the workforce grows at 2% and productivity at 4%, the economy would stabilise at 6% growth over time. And if the rate of labour productivity rises, according to this framework, growth in the economy rises pari passu (Graph 1a).

Between the three variables — output growth, labour growth and productivity growth — output growth adjusts to the other two. This is what Robert Solow, a celebrated economist and a Nobel laureate, showed in a seminal paper on growth theory. What he did not explain though was why and where did this labour productivity rise come from. Much later, his successors argued that the growth of labour productivity depends on investment in human capital, research and development, patent regimes, etc., what came to be known as endogenous growth theories.

A key expected impact of AI is an unprecedented rise in labour productivity, as its success as a technological revolution is premised on such an increase; what remains to be seen is how pervasive its impact will be across different sectors of the economy

Many have likened the artificial intelligence (AI) phenomenon to the inventions of the steam engine or internal combustion engine in the 18th and 19th centuries, respectively. Only time can tell whether AI is epochal of that kind. In this two-part piece, we discuss the possible impact it may have on the global economy as a whole.

A key impact of AI is considered to be an unprecedented rise in labour productivity. In fact, if there is one purpose AI is supposed to serve, it is enhancing labour productivity multifold. Since labour productivity is a key variable in this puzzle, consider what it constitutes of (Box 1) . It is a ratio of output and workers employed. Now this ratio can rise in three different ways — a rise in output for a given number of workers employed (rise in the numerator); a loss of jobs which leads to a fall in the denominator; more jobs are created, but the output rises faster than the jobs (while both the numerator and the denominator are rising, the numerator rises faster than the denominator).

There is usually a distinction drawn between a case where there is a net loss of jobs versus one where jobs grow, but the output grows even faster. The latter is preferred over the former. Even though AI may displace white-collar workers, it may generate more jobs for the blue-collar workers, so in the net there may not be a job loss with AI adoption across the economy. However, for the argument we make below, it does not matter which of the three sources leads to a rise in productivity. Why should the rise in labour productivity matter? There are two contrasting takes on this question in the economics discipline.

One which argues that productivity growth increases the growth of output in the economy. The idea is simple. Growth of output is a function of its two inputs — labour and capital. Since capital enhances the productivity of labour, the rate at which output can grow is the sum of the growth of the labour force and its productivity. So, if the workforce grows at 2% and productivity at 4%, the economy would stabilise at 6% growth over time. And if the rate of labour productivity rises, according to this framework, growth in the economy rises pari passu (Graph 1a).

Between the three variables — output growth, labour growth and productivity growth — output growth adjusts to the other two. This is what Robert Solow, a celebrated economist and a Nobel laureate, showed in a seminal paper on growth theory. What he did not explain though was why and where did this labour productivity rise come from. Much later, his successors argued that the growth of labour productivity depends on investment in human capital, research and development, patent regimes, etc., what came to be known as endogenous growth theories.

articles.title: Estonia to close border with Russia, Moscow decries 'new Iron Curtain'
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: NATO and EU member ‌Estonia on November 15 accused Russian security services of staging an attempted ‌arson ⁠attack on an Estonian defence company, in what it said ⁠was the second such incident this year

Estonia will close its road border crossings with Russia on security grounds for at least six months, the Baltic country's government ‌said on Friday (November 20, 2026), prompting a warning from Moscow that it would respond with political and diplomatic measures.

NATO and EU member ‌Estonia on Sunday (November 15, 2026) accused Russian security services of staging an attempted ‌arson ⁠attack on an Estonian defence company, in what it said ⁠was the second such incident this year.
This would help address the wider security situation and limit Russia's ability to ​organise further attacks, Estonian Interior Minister ‌Igor Taro told a press conference.
"Russian security services are intimidating and trying to recruit our citizens who are travelling through our border checkpoints. This is something we cannot tolerate anymore," Mr. Taro said.
The Kremlin has ‌denied any involvement in the weekend arson attack.
Foreign Ministry spokeswoman ​Maria Zakharova on Friday (November 20, 2026) said that Russia would respond with political and diplomatic measures if Estonia went ahead with the ⁠closure.
"Such moves are tantamount to attempts to erect a new Iron Curtain under the false pretence of some sort of threat from the East," ‌Ms. Zakharova said.
Estonia, a strong supporter of Ukraine, currently has five crossing points where travellers can enter or leave Russia, according to the government.
Estonia's northern neighbour Finland shut its Russia border crossings in 2023, and has kept them closed since then, while southern Baltic nations Latvia and Lithuania maintain open crossings.

Thousands of people living in Estonia have family in ‌Russia or vice versa, as legacies of the Soviet era. The crossing at Narva, a ​majority Russian-speaking city on the Estonian side of the border, is also used by people travelling from further afield in ⁠Europe to reach St. Petersburg a few hours' drive away.
Of the ⁠760,000 people who crossed the Estonia-Russia border this year, 307,000 were Russian nationals, 175,000 were Estonian citizens and 54,000 held Finnish ‌passports, Estonian police data showed.
Rail freight is not affected by the road closure, but remains subject to strict customs checks, Estonia said.

articles.title: Italian workers, students protest over wages and public services
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Parliament is examining Meloni's €26 billion ($30 billion) budget for 2027, which CGIL says does not go far enough to support incomes and public services

Tens of thousands of workers and ‌students took to the streets across Italy on Friday (November 20, 2026) as the country's largest ​trade union, CGIL, staged a general strike, demanding higher wages and greater investment in ⁠public services.

The demonstrations coincided with a broader wave of youth mobilisation across Europe. Student protests were also planned in Germany, France, Britain, Austria, Belgium and Spain over rising living costs and military spending.
"Today is also a very important ‌day because young people are taking to the streets not just in Italy but across Europe," CGIL leader Maurizio Landini said.
"Across Europe and among ordinary people, the demand ‌for change is growing," he added.

Other Italian unions, including the grassroots Cobas movement, also called for separate ‌strike ⁠action, while student demonstrations were planned nationwide amid simmering discontent over the policies of Prime ⁠Minister Giorgia Meloni's government.
The CGIL strike was scheduled to last the entire working day and involved workers in both the private and public sectors, including schools and healthcare.
Air and rail transport services were excluded from the general strike, while its ​impact on local public transport was limited by ‌minimum-service requirements.
However, a separate rail strike was due to begin at 9 p.m. (2000 GMT) on Friday (November 20, 2026) and run until 8 p.m. on Saturday (November 21, 2026).

Addressing a rally in Rome, Mr. Landini said more than one million people had taken part in demonstrations across more than 100 Italian cities. ‌The Interior Ministry said it was too early to provide its own estimate.
The protests come ​as Italy gears up for a parliamentary election due in 2027.

Friday's (November 20, 2026) demonstrations follow a nationwide mobilisation on October 30, when thousands ⁠of students joined striking workers to demand more funding for education and relief from rising living and housing costs.
Student groups have since continued protests and occupations at schools and universities, with opposition to higher military spending ‌also emerging as a rallying cry.

articles.title: Pakistan Army chief Munir vows to eliminate terrorism from country
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Pakistan overall witnessed a significant decline in terrorism-related violence during October, with attacks falling by 37%, deaths resulting from these attacks declining by 57%, and injuries decreasing by 71% compared to September, said Dawn newspaper report

Pakistan’s Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir on Friday (November 20, 2026) expressed the “unwavering resolve” of the security forces to eliminate terrorism from the country during a visit to the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.
Mr. Munir, who is also the Chief of Defence Forces (CDF), said this during a visit to Miranshah in North Waziristan district, the military's media wing said in a statement.

“He reaffirmed the unwavering resolve of the security forces, in close coordination with law enforcement agencies, to decisively eliminate the menace of terrorism and preserve the hard-earned peace and stability of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa,” the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement.
Mr. Munir also appreciated the KP police and expressed pride in its resilience and sacrifices against terrorism and Fitna-al-Khawarij.
The term Fitna-al-Khawarij is used by the federal government for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

During the visit, the CDF was given a comprehensive briefing on “the prevailing security situation, ongoing intelligence-based operations [IBO] and measures being undertaken to consolidate the gains achieved through sustained counter-terrorism efforts, “ the ISPR statement said.
It added that CDF Munir also interacted with officers and troops and appreciated their “high level of preparedness, professionalism and unwavering commitment".
Security forces continue to carry out counterterrorism action in KP and Balochistan, the two provinces that have been particularly affected by terrorism in Pakistan.
On Saturday (November 14, 2026), ISPR said four troops, including a major, were killed while 24 terrorists were killed in IBOs in Balochistan and KP’s North Waziristan.
Furthermore, last week, 74 terrorists were killed in IBOs in KP and Balochistan.

Meanwhile, the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies, an Islamabad-based independent think tank, has reported encouraging trends in the two provinces in its monthly assessment for October, the Dawn newspaper reported.

Pakistan overall witnessed a significant decline in terrorism-related violence during October, with attacks falling by 37%, deaths resulting from these attacks declining by 57%, and injuries decreasing by 71% compared to September, the report said.

articles.title: NIA sends request to UAE to probe any Indian footprints of copilot of flydubai flight who attacked Smit Machchhar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: “Who did the co-pilot come in contact with? Are there any Indian footprints of his friends circle who could be lurking. We will go ahead as soon as we get documents and permission from UAE to join the investigation,” says NIA chief

The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has sent a mutual legal assistance (MLA) request to the United Arab Emirates to probe any “Indian footprints” of the flydubai co-pilot who attacked Indian Captain Smit Machchhar in an apparent bid to crash the Israel-bound flight on September 30, 2026.

The first officer has been identified by the NIA as an Omani national in a First Information Report (FIR) filed by the NIA on October 9. The NIA registered the case as it involved the Indian national, Captain Machchhar.
NIA Director-General (D-G) Rakesh Aggarwal said on Friday that the MLAT request was made to the UAE to seek copies of certain documents and also permission to examine certain persons.

“There are issues of the co-pilot having studied in Australia and the U.K. Who did he come in contact with? Are there any Indian footprints of his friends circle who could be lurking. We will go ahead as soon as we get the documents and permission from the UAE to join the investigation,” Mr. Aggarwal said. The official said the NIA could investigate offences committed outside India under certain legal conditions.

“The NIA can investigate offences committed abroad if the act, had it been committed in India, would fall under offences that the NIA is empowered to investigate. Such investigations can proceed when: India’s interests are affected, or Indian citizens are involved, either as victims or in other capacities specified under the law,” he said.

Speaking on the conclusion of the two-day Anti-Terror Conference, the NIA-D-G said there had been a significant improvement in bringing back fugitives who had escaped to other countries. Since 1999, 303 fugitives had been brought back to the country.

“No fugitive who has committed any crime in India can find a safe haven anywhere in the world. For that, while the Government of India continues to engage with other countries to send these fugitives back, there is something which needs to be done by the agencies also, and that is proper documentation, so that the evidence against them is accepted by the foreign countries where these persons are residing and is upheld by their courts.”
He said that one of the six sessions was on international cooperation in combating cross-border terrorism involving mutual legal assistance treaty, letters rogatory and extradition requests.

“The main issue discussed was how we can use these channels more effectively. When we ask for somebody’s extradition, or we ask some other country to help us in the investigation of an offence, then whatever offence we are talking about should also be an offence in that country. Only then the request can be processed....Since there are different laws in different countries, sometimes the other country does not understand or is not able to appreciate which offence under Indian law corresponds to an offence in their country,” Mr. Aggarwal said.

He said extradition, deportation or any such movement ultimately depends on the legal process of another country, and the agencies must ensure that evidence and documentation met the legal standards required by foreign jurisdictions to support extradition and overseas investigations.
“Other than extradition, deportation is also a way to get back the fugitives and it can happen with diplomatic efforts,” the D-G said.

“The NIA can investigate offences committed abroad if the act, had it been committed in India, would fall under offences that the NIA is empowered to investigate. Such investigations can proceed when: India’s interests are affected, or Indian citizens are involved, either as victims or in other capacities specified under the law,” he said.

Speaking on the conclusion of the two-day Anti-Terror Conference, the NIA-D-G said there had been a significant improvement in bringing back fugitives who had escaped to other countries. Since 1999, 303 fugitives had been brought back to the country.

“No fugitive who has committed any crime in India can find a safe haven anywhere in the world. For that, while the Government of India continues to engage with other countries to send these fugitives back, there is something which needs to be done by the agencies also, and that is proper documentation, so that the evidence against them is accepted by the foreign countries where these persons are residing and is upheld by their courts.”

He said that one of the six sessions was on international cooperation in combating cross-border terrorism involving mutual legal assistance treaty, letters rogatory and extradition requests.

“The main issue discussed was how we can use these channels more effectively. When we ask for somebody’s extradition, or we ask some other country to help us in the investigation of an offence, then whatever offence we are talking about should also be an offence in that country. Only then the request can be processed....Since there are different laws in different countries, sometimes the other country does not understand or is not able to appreciate which offence under Indian law corresponds to an offence in their country,” Mr. Aggarwal said.

He said extradition, deportation or any such movement ultimately depends on the legal process of another country, and the agencies must ensure that evidence and documentation met the legal standards required by foreign jurisdictions to support extradition and overseas investigations.

“Other than extradition, deportation is also a way to get back the fugitives and it can happen with diplomatic efforts,” the D-G said.

articles.title: U.S. sanctions Myanmar armed group leader over scam links
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Treasury Department said on November 19 it had imposed an asset freeze on General Saw Shwe Wah, commander-in-chief of the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA), and one of his top officers, and had banned Americans from dealing with them
The United States has frozen the assets of the leader of an ethnic armed group in Myanmar and one of his lieutenants, accusing them of facilitating cyberscammers who target Americans.

Organised criminal gangs have, for years, carried out fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes from compounds in Southeast Asian nations, defrauding victims around the world of tens of billions of dollars annually.
The industry is adapting its operations in the wake of much-publicised crackdowns in Myanmar and Cambodia following Chinese pressure, often dissipating into smaller facilities in new locations.

The U.S. Treasury Department said on Thursday (November 19, 2026) it had imposed an asset freeze on General Saw Shwe Wah, commander-in-chief of the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA), and one of his top officers, and had banned Americans from dealing with them.
The DKBA is one of the myriad armed groups operating in Myanmar's borderlands, some of which have been fighting the government for decades.
It has signed a ceasefire with Yangon and is accused by the United States, which earlier sanctioned the organisation, of supporting scam centres.

"DKBA actors not only provide security for scam compounds and permit their continued operation, but also actively participate in violence against victims of human trafficking trapped inside the compounds," the U.S. Treasury said.
The DKBA's Colonel Saw A One, responsible for security in the Three Pagodas Pass area in Karen State near the Thai border, was also designated by the U.S. on Thursday (November 19, 2026).
Jason Tower, senior expert at the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime, told that last week the Three Pagodas Pass region has been a "major expansion area" for scam compounds.
The latest U.S. Treasury measures also sanctioned Zhao Hui, a China-born, naturalised Cambodian accused of running cyberscam compounds in Cambodia, and two of his companies.
Mr. Zhao, 35, also leased a scam centre owned by the Cambodian conglomerate Prince Group, which Washington accuses of running a multibillion-dollar scam operation, the Treasury said in a statement.
Prince's China-born founder Chen Zhi was extradited by Phnom Penh to China in January, months after the conglomerate was sanctioned by the U.S. and U.K. governments for scamming.

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition says targeted Yemen's Hodeida, other attacks 'ongoing'
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: We targeted operational capabilities at Hodeidah port that were used in smuggling operations and the transport of weapons and ballistic missiles, said spokesman
The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said it targeted Hodeida port and other sites around the country on Friday (November 20, 2026), after the group warned of widespread reprisals.

"We targeted operational capabilities at Hodeidah port that were used in smuggling operations and the transport of weapons and ballistic missiles," spokesman Turki al-Malki posted on X, adding that operations were "ongoing" in Sanaa, Saada and Taiz governorates.

articles.title: Millions of students take NEET, yet hundreds of medical seats go vacant
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Under the 2026 Float and Freeze option, candidates can carry forward their allotments without completing admission formalities, and even if their seats remain unchanged in Round 3, they can choose not to join; this flexibility has had significant implications in seat utilisation

Even as millions of candidates competed for admission, several undergraduate MBBS seats remained vacant during the NEET-UG 2026 counselling. Over 3,000-3,400 vacancies were reported after the initial All India Quota (AIQ) and State rounds, with approximately 410 seats still unfilled in deemed universities even after the Special Stray Vacancy Round.
(Sign up for THEdge , The Hindu’s weekly education newsletter.)

While government medical college seats were all filled, most remaining vacancies were in deemed universities. States such as Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karnataka accounted for a significant share of these vacancies, raising concerns about high fees, seat utilisation and equitable access to medical education.

As per the data published by the National Medical Commission (NMC), the total number of MBBS seats available in the country for the academic session 2026–27 stands at 1,40,664. Of these, 64,121 seats are available in government medical colleges, while the remaining 76,543 seats are in the private medical sector. The latter comprises 14,299 seats in deemed university medical colleges and 62,244 seats in self-financing private medical colleges. Thus, more than 54% of the total MBBS seats in the country are concentrated in the private medical sector, where the cost of medical education is generally substantially higher than in government institutions.

The National Testing Agency (NTA) reported that 11,21,185 candidates qualified NEET-UG 2026 by securing marks above the prescribed category-wise qualifying cut-off. This included 9,96,935 candidates belonging to the General/EWS qualifying category, and 1,24,250 candidates belonging to the OBC, SC and ST categories who qualified with scores ranging from 177 to 212 marks.

articles.title: Three to tango: On Trump, Xi, Putin trilateral summit
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: U.S., China, Russia must draw up a roadmap for talks on nuclear weapons

The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.

Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

Editorial Context: Three to tango: On Trump, Xi, Putin trilateral summit. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

• U.S., China, Russia must draw up a roadmap for talks on nuclear weapons
• The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.
• Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

articles.title: Going public on AI: On Anthropic IPO
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India can no longer afford its silence on the multi-trillion dollar AI arms race

The Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Anthropic , PBC is a mile marker in the arms race to develop superintelligent systems driven by generative AI . Traders valued the firm at $1.27 trillion, a denomination that is bound to become more and more familiar in an industry backed by an endless appetite for capital and unprecedented forms of financialisation. Anthropic’s statements emphasise warnings on the safety of its systems and the consequences of unbridled development of advanced systems. In the history of the development of this technology, this PR spin may just be a blip. After all, their testing has led to AI agents that have broken out of sandboxes and infected unsuspecting organisations’ internal systems: a deluge of agentic chaos that is already a reality has led to little signs of the firm backing its words with action. A familiar trend is playing out, with open source LLMs showing frontier capabilities that can back their erratic impulses, appearing in the space of just months, or sometimes weeks. Advocates of pacing the frontier and managing these emerging risks have been marginalised in a way that has little precedent in this century. It is time for governments to get involved, and specifically, for India to raise its voice on these risks, loudly and unequivocally.

While India’s AI industry is nascent, its positions on international forums carry the weight of a sixth of humanity. A mix of cynical calculations and practical considerations have blunted the use of that voice, for example in the U.S.’s hugely destabilising war of choice against Iran, and Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza. In taking a strong position on what could be the defining transformation of this decade, India has little to lose, and a lot to contribute. India’s AI policies are geared towards diffusion and research of helpful capabilities that can trickle down to the common citizen. The capabilities that the Union government and State governments seek to boost by leveraging AI are removed from the frontier research wreaking havoc within the information security profession around the world. Out-of-control AI agents promise, moreover, significant disruption to outdated government and private systems online. While India has little commercial leverage to curb San Francisco’s accelerationism, its voice is sure to be noticed. India’s focus on AI in international fora, such as the AI Impact Summit in Delhi, has been on consensus. This approach must change. India cannot be silent amid a U.S.-China technological race which could lead to catastrophic damage. New Delhi must not allow the U.S. to stop it from pushing for AI safety.

articles.title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah to visit India on November 22-23
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: In his first India visit, Nepal Prime Minister is expected to sign several MoUs and inaugurate projects
Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will visit India on November 22-23, the Ministry of External Affairs announced on Friday (November 20, 2026).
Briefing the media in Kathmandu, Nepal’s Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai said Mr. Shah will be accompanied by a 34-member delegation.

#WATCH | Kathmandu | "On the invitation of the Prime Minister of India, Nepali PM Balendra Shah will embark on a State visit to India from 22nd to 23rd November," says Nepal's Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai. He adds, "It will be a 34-member government team that will depart from Kathmandu to New Delhi, India. During the visit, the Nepali PM will hold a delegation-level meeting on Monday with his Indian counterpart. Various projects relating to energy will be inaugurated by the two Prime Ministers. Various aspects of cooperation will be signed and exchanged. After the delegation-level talks, the two Prime Ministers will hold a joint press conference. Nepali PM will also call on the President of India, Droupadi Murmu. Nepali PM will also lay a wreath at Mahatma Gandhi's memorial at Rajghat. Nepali PM will also attend the Nepal-India Business Forum."

“Bilateral cooperation has witnessed progress across diverse sectors, including trade and commerce, development partnership, energy and water resources, and physical and digital connectivity, with growing engagement in newer areas such as start-ups, technology and innovation, and sports,” the Ministry said.

This will be the Nepal Prime Minister’s first visit to India since he took charge last March. Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal, who both visited India earlier this year, will join the delegation.
Official spokesperson for the Ministry of External Affairs Randhir Jaiswal said Mr. Shah’s trip will be a “state visit, during which he will be accorded state honours”.

“He will meet with our President and hold discussions with our Prime Minister. Given that this is a highly multifaceted relationship, the talks will cover a wide range of topics, including our development partnership, economic cooperation, and various other matters,” said Mr. Jaiswal during the biweekly media briefing on Friday (November 20, 2026).

Mr. Rai said the two countries are expected to sign several memorandums of understanding covering different areas of cooperation, and a few completed projects are expected to be inaugurated following PM Balendra Shah’s meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Sources said the Dharchula Bridge, the land port of Banbasa at the Uttarakhand-Nepal border, and a train route between Janakpur and Gorakhpur are slated to be opened.

Earlier this month, India’s Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri visited Kathmandu. India’s External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar will be the first government representative to call on Prime Minister Shah upon his arrival on Sunday (November 22, 2026). Formal engagements will begin Monday morning with a ceremonial reception at the Rashtrapati Bhavan, followed by a visit to Rajghat, where Mr. Shah will lay a wreath at Mahatma Gandhi’s memorial. He will then meet Prime Minister Modi at Hyderabad House, where the MoUs will be signed. He will leave for Kathmandu later that afternoon.

The former media figure and rapper-turned-Prime Minister took office after the Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) won the election following the overthrow of Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli’s government during the Gen-Z uprising in Kathmandu in September 2025.
Rastriya Swatantra Party chief Rabi Lamichhane was hosted in New Delhi earlier this summer. He also visited Uttarakhand and Assam in October for a pilgrimage to Kainchi Dham and the Kamakhya temple.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: The ECI offers relief to a section of deleted electors but SIR’s flaws remain

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in some States that had undergone the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) , mostly in Phases 1 and 2, some 74 lakh names were added onto the electoral rolls. This meant that the electorate in those 13 States, that had shrunk from 49.61 crore to 45.22 crore after the SIR, has now gone up to 45.96 crore. The ECI has extended the SSR to States and UTs in Phase 3. As before, it requires no proof of citizenship or mapping to older rolls, and insists on personal notice before any deletion other than of the dead. It also directs Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to cross-verify deletions personally wherever they exceed 2% of a polling station’s electors. Draft deletions in Phase 3 of the SIR averaged 17% , and reached 32.8% in Delhi . The ECI also offered another opportunity to electors deleted by the SIR in the seven States and UTs where it is still underway, such as Delhi and Maharashtra, to return to the rolls. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address.
